title: [Experiment] Train a Transformer for its fixed TL3 blend contribution on B300
body:
# [Experiment] Train a Transformer for its fixed contribution to clean TL3

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Implemented receiver handoff, `REMOTE_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING`; zero new fits or local model executions. H-B300-TL3-TRANSFORMER-COMPLEMENT-20261106 / E-B300-TL3-TRANSFORMER-COMPLEMENT-20261106. Owner: team kotiki / receiving B300 operator. Target `research-team`, base `7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d`. This is a teacher/blend-connection experiment extending PR38's frozen-parent correction family and PR49/52/53 evidence. Published as [draft PR #67](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/67); implementation commit `7f660553a1df3066f2e735e8975b39c225ec9870`. The receiver must pin that exact reviewed commit or a separately reviewed successor. Canonical trainer, reference bridge, four configs, acceptance/profiles, evaluation and comparison are implemented; GPU acceptance is not executed.

2. **Why it should work.** Stronger standalone candidates have not reliably improved TL3 mixtures. Train z against the actual fixed endpoint `0.9*b + 0.1*z`, with unchanged original clipped-label weights/mask and the WMSE numerator scaled by `1/0.1²`. Control trains z on labels; both are scored as the same fixed blend. This is weighted residual-target regression, not a new boosting algorithm. Scaling matches output curvature only; gradient scale, clipping and Muon/AdamW trajectories remain different. A paired blend advantage is the predicted observation. In-sample reference optimism or changed optimization dynamics are strong alternatives; all-seed contrasts and gradient/profile diagnostics constrain interpretation.

3. **Compute advantage.** Four T768×24 / context 1024 / 30-epoch fits on eight B300s target complementary capacity, reusing a 17-role historical clean TL3 lineage. Historical reuse costs are distinct from four new fits; six native reference exports, checks, twelve short profiles and evaluation add non-fitting compute. Hardware is available according to the user, but GPU-hours, peak memory and throughput are unmeasured. More training compute does not relax CPU serving limits; compact distillation is deferred, separately budgeted and not implemented in this packet. Opportunity cost is four full Transformer fits rather than another broad architecture/mixture sweep.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Two arms × seeds 101001/101002 share one exact PR49 train-only source split (SHA256 `0c4de3a253d23b3a5d5ca73b7aeb7fcae2b974673e4f9ec51e94e593c59d114c`), full 10,325 fitting train sequences, zero fitting valid, 1,873 evaluation valid. `expected_fold=0` is an identifier, not F0/F2 CV. Same physical eight-GPU/software identity, raw112 fitting-only normalization, width 768 / layers 24 / heads 12 / FF 4, context 1024 / chunk 256, batch 1/rank, accumulation 4, 30 epochs, Muon LR 3e-4 / momentum 0.95 / NS 5 / epsilon 1e-7 plus AdamW betas 0.9/0.95 / epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0.01, 5% warmup/cosine/minimum ratio 0.1, gradient clipping 1, dropout 0 and fixed final epoch 30. BF16/BF16x9 follows the explicit user precision amendment; it is not strict IEEE FP32. No KD/hints, no component preclipping, no alpha/epoch search. Treatment references are detached and separately identified; legacy default/KD math remains unchanged. Resume requires exact source/config/data/runtime state.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** `labels_s101001`, `complement_s101001`, `labels_s101002`, `complement_s101002`: two fits per arm, four new fits total / 120 model-epochs; no new reference-teacher or student fits. All endpoints are 0.9 frozen clean TL3 + 0.1 z. Reuse exact PR49 W18 ep 1 (.34) and tiedlead_s5/s6 ep 3 (.33/.33), verified through all 17 published checkpoint/provenance pins. The old public-best/all-labels weights are not valid substitutes. The two seeds share one fitting/evaluation split and reference; they are not two independent datasets. No automatic follow-up allocation or queue.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Canonical pooled `global_wp_clip2_v1`, official scored mask after warmup, clipping after composition. Baseline replay must reproduce 0.6923774245652725 within 2e-6 before profiles/fits. Report each arm versus TL3 and treatment versus matched control, both seeds, no best-seed selection. Paired whole-component bootstrap uses 2,000 draws / RNG 271828 and conditions on fixed fitted predictors. Official valid is development-exposed; two seeds do not establish statistical significance, reliable training variance or public/private transfer. The current portal team best 0.66832 and leader 0.67596 are distinct public observations, not this validation scale.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Preserve the original source manifest, source/index metadata and component exclusions; never repair mismatches by rebuilding the split. Native replay uses clean commit `c42baf7b95946994216801b4eb9909422ea7effa`. Full prediction rows are joined by source-qualified group ID, cache arrays/metadata and ancestry hashes are verified, and explicit evaluation composition rejects a different fit reference. Inputs/reset are causal, normalization fitting-only, original labels supply objective weights. Limitations remain: fitting references are in-sample, not OOF; historical consumed training-cache bytes are not independently reconstructed despite published17-role ancestry pins; official valid is exposed; calendar chronology is unavailable. These limits are recorded in cache identity and the research contract.

8. **Decision-changing result.** A follow-up-budget trigger requires mean treatment-minus-TL3 ≥ +0.0005, nonnegative treatment-minus-TL3 for each seed, and nonnegative treatment-minus-label-blend for each matched seed. Passing only motivates a separately frozen confirmation/serving experiment; no additional fit or submission launches automatically. Mixed or small positive evidence is inconclusive. Consistent negative evidence narrows this fixed recipe; a zero-crossing conditional interval alone does not kill Transformers. Selection cost and failures remain in the record.

9. **How to run.** Exact receiver commands and absolute-path bindings are in `research/experiment_drafts/tl3-transformer-complement-20261106/README.md`. Provision from committed lock, stage 17 hash-pinned checkpoint/provenance pairs from PR49/52 archives, preserve canonical data/index metadata and split, create clean exact-c42 legacy checkout, then `data-check` → six explicit one-GPU `reference-export` calls → `reference-import` → `baseline-score` → `check`. Check runs BF16 and BF16x9 GPU objective cases in separate processes, default/treatment two-rank DDP and Muon checks. For each declared cell: `profile-one`, `profile-eight`, `profile-peak`; a receiving reviewer inspects actual headroom/finite losses and approves a copy of the unchanged production receipt; then `fit`, `evaluate`, `bundle`. `compare` requires all four. `resume` uses exact cell training state. No live job is modified; no local tests/training/inference/profiles were run. Real-shape resource acceptance remains missing until the receiver performs it.

10. **Evidence to return.** Per-cell config/source/runtime/data/normalization/reference provenance; all-rank logs; original/scaled/composite losses, LR, preclip norms/clipping/nonfinite events, completed work/time/memory; terminal status; explicit composed prediction manifest and canonical score; all three profiles and approved production copy. Return separate evidence/weights archives with SHA256 and access locations. Retain shared data/acceptance/baseline/comparison receipts and reference manifests/export provenance as companion evidence; the per-cell bundle does not contain all shared cache arrays. No dataset publishing, CPU-ready ZIP or compact-KD claim.

11. **Results and trace.** See packet `SUBMISSION_AUDIT.md` for all 108 team submission entries reviewed and the public frontier, `reference_sources/README.md` for primary artifact receipts, `recipe.json` for frozen budget and endpoints, append-only H/E ledgers and unified idea/review/source indices. Independent static criticism prompted strict reference ancestry, curvature scaling, profile-schema preservation and fail-closed composition. Static checks support implementation review only. Every fit/profile score is pending; there is no measured new quality, throughput, CPU acceptance or leaderboard gain. Publication is [draft PR #67](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/67) at implementation commit `7f660553a1df3066f2e735e8975b39c225ec9870`; merge and receiver archives remain absent. See packet `PUBLICATION.json` and `VALIDATION.json`.

title: [Experiment] Matched-budget Transformer SwiGLU and compact teacher transfer on B300
body:
# [Experiment] Matched-budget Transformer SwiGLU and compact teacher transfer on B300

Implementation and receiver launch packet are published in [draft PR #66](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/66); receiver acceptance is pending. [Full launch commands and frozen panel](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/transformer-swiglu-20261106/research/experiment_drafts/transformer-swiglu-20261106/README.md). Implementation commit: `0531c33048a335059f7bb4fb6a4d2874c48ffcdb`. No local tests, training, inference, profiles or scoring ran. This packet records the earlier SwiGLU mechanism proposed in the [causal Transformer plan](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d/research/unified/ideas/CAUSAL_AR_TRANSFORMER_GRU_DISTILLATION_B300_20261017_R1.md) and [large dynamics plan](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d/research/unified/ideas/LARGE_DYNAMICS_TRANSFORMER_B300_20261019_R2.md). It does not claim a novel architecture or a quality result.

1. **Status and lineage.** `H-B300-TRANSFORMER-SWIGLU-20261106` and `E-B300-TRANSFORMER-SWIGLU-20261106` are a bounded implementation of the planned gated FFN in the present GELU-only sequence Transformer. The branch starts from `research-team` commit `7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d`. Historical configs that omit `ff_activation` and `ff_hidden` retain their config fields, GELU parameter names/order, state-dict structure and forward path. The two optional keys are not injected into historical defaults.

2. **Mechanism, prediction and falsifier.** The reference uses `GELU(up(norm(x)))`; the candidate uses `SiLU(gate(norm(x))) * up(norm(x))`, followed by the existing down projection. For this causal numerical teacher, predict a positive matched-fold difference in fixed-final pooled weighted Pearson correlation (WP). A mean SwiGLU-minus-GELU teacher difference below `+0.0005`, a fold regression, or failed receiver admission fails this specific allocation trigger. A negative screen narrows this width/schedule/precision recipe; it does not falsify all gated FFNs.

3. **Matching and planned cost.** At hidden width 768, the GELU inner width is 3072 and the SwiGLU inner width is 2048. Each has 4,718,592 FFN matrix weights per block and equal leading dense FFN matrix-multiply work per token. This does not match total parameters, bias count, elementwise work, optimizer operations or wall time: SwiGLU adds 1,024 bias scalars per layer, SiLU and multiplication, and one additional independently optimized matrix. Four new teacher fits are planned (two folds × two arms), 30 epochs each, 120 teacher epochs total, with no inherited fit endpoints. A separate allocation would fund four one-B300 students, 120 additional epochs, with zero reused endpoints.

4. **Frozen teacher recipe.** The four committed configs use T768×24, 12 heads, context 1024, chunk 256, batch 1/rank, accumulation 4, eight B300 ranks, Muon peak LR `3e-4`, momentum `.95`, five Newton–Schulz steps, 5% warmup and `warmup_cosine_v2` to `.1×` peak. Matrix decay is `.01`, clipping is 1, dropout is zero, and endpoint is configured final epoch 29. Training and normalization use each fold's complete fitting membership (`normalization_scope=all_fit`); output caches contain no hidden hints. The paired arms use the same fold and seed, schedule, membership and evaluation. Changed FFN shapes consume different random draws, so paired seeds do not imply bitwise-matched initial tensors.

5. **Precision and runtime.** The explicit recipe is BF16 autocast with BF16x9 cuBLAS emulation, using FP32 master parameters, gradients/accumulation, loss, optimizer state and exported predictions. Exact-window efficient attention and compiled blocks are explicit. This follows the [24 October precision amendment](../b300-transformer-distillation-runtime/PRECISION_AMENDMENT_20261024.md); BF16x9 is not IEEE-FP32 parity and can affect Muon GEMMs. No throughput or memory-fit claim is made.

6. **Follow-up students.** Only after a separate allocation, profile review and passing teacher-cache gates, four T128×2 GELU students may be fit: F0/seed 1001 and F2/seed 1002 from each teacher family. Within each fold both teacher arms use the same student config and seed. Each student uses one B300, context 128, 30 epochs, AdamW `3e-4`, BF16/BF16x9, `normalization_scope=all_fit`, no hidden hints and equal label/output-KD weights (`kd_weight=1`, `hint_weight=0`). This compares the resulting student quality under these teacher caches. There is no labels-only student arm, so it does not estimate KD benefit against labels alone. The one/eight-rank cache exports must cover exactly the current fold's train and validation groups, bind the selected teacher checkpoint/config/source, and pass full-array parity before students can proceed.

7. **Leakage and endpoint.** The canonical source-qualified F0/F2 split remains fixed. Teacher training and normalization use only complete fitting membership; the teacher cache exporter emits `membership=fit`; student training consumes that cache and its own fold's fitting labels. Evaluation uses the existing canonical scored mask and pooled WP metric. The final configured epoch is fixed before outer scoring; no outer score chooses an epoch. F0/F2 are exposed development groups, not a newly pristine holdout.

8. **Comparison and uncertainty.** `compare_scores.py` validates identical split hashes, official metric identity, component IDs and component-centered moments, reproduces both pooled WP scores, and reports a deterministic 2,000-draw paired component bootstrap for each fold. The panel decision uses the arithmetic mean of the two fixed teacher-fold differences and requires both nonnegative plus mean at least `+0.0005`. Two exposed fold/seed cells cannot identify seed variability, establish statistical significance, separate fold from seed, or estimate public transfer; component intervals are conditional on these fits.

9. **Receiver acceptance and admission.** On the allocated Linux host, run the receiver check stage before profiles: focused sequence invariants, existing sequence contracts/recovery/Muon tests, two-rank DDP, and two-rank FP32 Muon checks for both FFNs. Then profile each teacher cell at one/eight ranks with its production config and at eight ranks with warmup zero; profile each student config at one rank with production and peak-LR variants only if the follow-up is separately authorized. Inspect actual B300/software, split/source/config identities, finite losses and optimizer states, completed update counts, and memory by rank with at least 20% device-memory headroom. Preserve every original `approved:false` receipt. A human reviewer may copy only the identity-matching production receipt to `approved_profile.json` and set `approved=true` with a review note: teacher uses the exact eight-rank production profile; student uses the exact one-rank production profile. The trainer validates the approved receipt against the full fit identity; a peak-LR or alternate-world-size receipt cannot authorize the full fit.

10. **Execution and artifacts.** `run.sh` exposes explicit single-stage commands and fixed cell names. It has no queue, loop over scientific cells, profile bypass or automatic approval. Set `WNN_EXPECTED_COMMIT`, canonical data/split paths, a receiver-reviewed persistent disk `WNN_RUN_ROOT` and exact allocated device IDs. Run `bash "$PACKET/run.sh" check`; it records `findmnt`, `df` and `lsblk` evidence for a human storage-capacity review. Then use one reviewed cell per stage (`teacher-profile-one`, `teacher-profile-eight`, `teacher-profile-peak`, manual approval, `teacher-fit`, `teacher-evaluate`, `teacher-cache-one`, `teacher-cache-eight`, `teacher-cache-parity`, `teacher-bundle`). Repeat explicitly for the other three teacher cells. Run `compare_scores.py` once per fold after both scores exist. The separately allocated student route uses `student-profile-one`, `student-profile-peak`, manual approval, `student-fit`, `student-evaluate` and `student-bundle`; cache bindings are revalidated against the actual current split, full committed recipe, source, checkpoint, parity receipt and manifests before each stage. Teacher result bundles include fit evidence and weights, all production/peak profile receipts, approved-profile copy, cache manifests and parity receipt. Student bundles include fit evidence and weights, its profiles, approved-profile copy, and the stage binding receipts embedding the parity receipt. Preserve the receiver acceptance bundle alongside these cell bundles.

11. **Evidence and limits.** Static source/config review and Ruff/shell syntax checks are the only local validation. New receiver tests and DDP checks are definitions for remote execution and remain unrun. No B300 acceptance, numerical parity, successful compile, fit, score, cache export, memory fit, quality improvement or throughput result is established. The paper [“GLU Variants Improve Transformer”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05202) motivates testing gated FFNs in its reported sequence-to-sequence setting; its results do not establish gains on this numerical competition. The `+0.0005` threshold is only a trigger for considering a separately allocated student panel.

title: [Experiment] Transformer SDPA gates, 1.54B scale and compact teacher transfer on B300
body:
Launch packet: [README and commands](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/tree/codex/transformer-sdpa-gate-20261106/research/experiment_drafts/transformer-sdpa-gate-20261106).

# [Experiment] E-B300-SDPA-GATE-20261106: query-dependent SDPA head gate

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Implementation and GPU handoff are published in [draft PR #65](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/65); GPU execution remains pending. Implementation commit: `a24c2c2bc3bea07ce1ce5711194fe5574e701c5b`. Hypothesis `H-B300-SDPA-GATE-20261106`; experiment `E-B300-SDPA-GATE-20261106`; lineage `causal_transformer_attention_gate`; owner: research-team experiment author. The branch is `codex/transformer-sdpa-gate-20261106`, based on `research-team` SHA `7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d`. The full implementation commit is the reviewed branch head supplied as `WNN_EXPECTED_COMMIT` on the receiver. The [existing large-dynamics proposal](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/transformer-sdpa-gate-20261106/research/unified/ideas/LARGE_DYNAMICS_TRANSFORMER_B300_20261019_R2.md) already listed a post-attention sigmoid gate as a candidate; this packet makes it executable. No local tests, model imports, profiles, fits, inference, cache exports or GPU actions ran.

2. **Why it should work.** A per-query, per-head sigmoid can suppress attention writes that are unhelpful for a row while retaining the existing causal attention and output projection. The implementation applies `sigmoid(W norm_attention(x) + b)` after SDPA and before the output projection. Both new tensors start at zero, so headwise starts at a uniform 0.5 multiplier. The paper [Gated Attention for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708) motivates this placement in LLMs; it does not establish benefit for this forecasting task. The strongest alternative is that any gain comes from constant attention attenuation. `constant_half` tests that alternative; `headwise - constant_half` is the query-dependence contrast.

3. **Compute advantage.** The added treatment uses one `heads × hidden` matrix and one head bias per block and adds a small projection/multiply around the existing SDPA. It reuses the same data, optimizer and 30-epoch schedule, so eight B300s test the quality effect without first allocating more model capacity. The initial width-768/depth-24 teacher is about 170M trunk parameters by architecture arithmetic. A separate conditional four-fit scale panel uses width 1792, depth 40, 28 heads and FF width 7168 (about 1.54B parameters by arithmetic); that count and its memory/throughput are not measured. If initial headwise teacher targets appear useful, a separately allocated four-student endpoint tests whether the difference transfers to a small Transformer. No wall-time, memory, scaling or public-score benefit is assumed.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Initial arms are `none`, `constant_half`, and `headwise`, matched within F0/seed101001 and F2/seed101002. The model is a raw112 causal Transformer, width768, depth24, 12 heads, FF3072, context1024, chunk256, dropout0, no hints, efficient exact-window SDPA and compiled blocks. Training is 30 epochs on the complete source-qualified fitting membership, `normalization_scope=all_fit`, `training_mask=all_after_warmup`, fixed final epoch29, no outer-fold checkpoint selection. All configs use 8 B300 ranks, per-rank batch1, accumulation4, Muon with peak LR3e-4, momentum.95, five FP32 Newton–Schulz rounds, auxiliary AdamW beta(.9,.95), matrix weight decay.01, no vector/bias decay, clip1, warmup.05 and `warmup_cosine_v2` to a .1 floor. `bf16_bf16x9` is explicit: BF16 forward autocast with FP32 master parameters, gradients, loss and optimizer state; set `CUBLAS_EMULATE_SINGLE_PRECISION=1`. This is not an IEEE-FP32 parity claim. The efficient-mask/compiler path must pass the receiver check and profile; no fallback may change one arm alone. KV state remains the canonical bounded cache and resets per sequence.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** The initial screen costs 6 new teacher fits: 2 per arm, 3 arms × F0/F2. There are no reused endpoints or shared-control substitutions. Profiles, DDP checks and one/eight-rank cache parity are engineering work, not fits. Conditional scale follow-up costs 4 additional fits (none/headwise × F0/F2) and is not included in the initial six or auto-started. Conditional student transfer costs 4 more fits (none-teacher/headwise-teacher × F0/F2), with a separate one-B300 student config for each fold, seeds1001/1002, width128, depth2, four heads, context128, output KD weight1, no hints, 30 epochs, AdamW and the same BF16/BF16x9 mode. Each student's profile and fit route the identical teacher cache. Students use only the initial width768 teachers; scale-teacher transfer is not allocated. Total if every separate stage is later admitted: 14 new fits (6 initial + 4 scale + 4 students), profiles excluded. Current executed fit/profile count is zero.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Primary outcome is the canonical pooled `global_wp_clip2_v1` on the official `is_scored & row>=99` mask, scored after fixed final checkpoints. Report every per-target and aggregate paired delta on identical F0/F2 components and the descriptive equal-cell mean. F0/F2 are exposed. Each fold has one fitting seed; fold and seed effects are confounded. A component-paired bootstrap, if reported, describes evaluation sensitivity conditional on the two fitted endpoints and is not a training-variance interval. Report source/regime/sequence-age slices as diagnostics without selecting a new winner after seeing them. No significance claim is available from this screen.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Inputs are the existing observed raw112 rows; no future competition labels enter features or autoregressive feedback. Fitting-only normalization is explicitly `all_fit`. The trainer enforces component-clean outer folds and the expected fold in each config; receiver review must verify the actual canonical split manifests and data identities. Teacher caches export only each teacher's fitting membership. They are in-sample teacher predictions on the teacher's own fitting rows, not cross-fitted targets. The evaluation fold remains excluded from teacher fitting/cache, but that does not remove teacher overfit from training targets. The transfer panel is therefore about downstream student quality under these cache semantics. All cited folds have previous exposure; no pristine holdout or future-regime claim follows.

8. **Decision-changing result.** A mean headwise-minus-none gain of at least `+0.0005 WP` with both fold deltas nonnegative is a predeclared exploratory follow-up trigger, not significance. Apply the same descriptive rule to headwise-teacher versus none-teacher students when those four fits are separately admitted. A query-dependent mechanism claim additionally needs positive `headwise - constant_half` deltas on both folds. If constant-half matches or beats headwise, the evidence supports simple attenuation at most; any attenuation follow-up needs a separate allocation, and there is no automatic 1.54B gate promotion. A negative, mixed, or small result narrows this exact model/optimizer/precision panel; it does not refute all gated attention. Scale and student stages each require a separate explicit allocation even if a trigger is met. Any failed receiver check/profile blocks fitting until a matched, reviewed source/config amendment; do not downgrade backend, compiler, precision, or one arm independently.

9. **How to run.** On the allocated Linux receiver, use a clean checkout of the reviewed full commit, `uv sync --frozen`, and the environment below. `run.sh` requires actual data/split paths, a dedicated physical-disk run root, full expected commit SHA and exact visible device IDs; it rejects wrong folds, unsupported device counts, dirty runtime sources and reused stage outputs. It is a thin, explicit CLI over canonical sequence trainer/predictor/scorer and result bundler scripts. There is no queue, automatic fit, or approval mutation.

   ```bash
   PACKET=research/experiment_drafts/transformer-sdpa-gate-20261106
   export WNN_EXPECTED_COMMIT='<reviewed full 40-character commit SHA>'
   export WNN_DATA_ROOT='/actual/canonical/data/root'
   export WNN_SPLIT_F0='/actual/canonical/f0.json'
   export WNN_SPLIT_F2='/actual/canonical/f2.json'
   export WNN_RUN_ROOT='/actual/physical-disk/sdpa-gate-20261106'
   export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='<exact eight allocated B300 IDs or UUIDs>'
   export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" check

   CELL=none_f0
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" profile "$CELL"
   # Human reviewer copies profile_receipt.json to approved_profile.json,
   # sets approved=true, and records reviewer and review note in the copy.
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" fit "$CELL"
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" evaluate "$CELL"
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" cache "$CELL"
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" cache-parity "$CELL"
   bash "$PACKET/run.sh" bundle "$CELL"
   ```

   Repeat profile, fit, evaluate and bundle explicitly for the other five initial cells, one at a time. Export and parity-check fitting caches for the `none` and `headwise` arms if the student follow-up is separately admitted; students do not consume `constant_half` caches. The emitted profile receipt is `approved=false`; only a separately reviewed `approved_profile.json` is accepted by the trainer. Conditional scale uses `scale-profile`, `scale-fit`, `scale-evaluate`, `scale-cache`, `scale-cache-parity`, and `scale-bundle` with `scale_none_f0`, `scale_none_f2`, `scale_headwise_f0`, or `scale_headwise_f2`; those commands write under `scale-teachers/`. For student cells, bind `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to one B300 and run `student-profile`, `student-fit`, `student-evaluate`, and `student-bundle` with one of `none_f0`, `headwise_f0`, `none_f2`, `headwise_f2`. The wrapper routes the exact matching initial teacher cache and refuses a cache without a passing one/eight-rank receipt bound to that teacher checkpoint, fold, arm and manifest. Failed outputs are preserved; use a new run root for a diagnosed retry.

10. **Evidence to return.** Preserve source/config/split/data/cache/runtime hashes; the original unapproved profile receipt and reviewer-created approved copy; all receiver tests and two-rank DDP receipts; eight-rank device topology, memory and compiled-backend logs; fit metadata, all rank logs, per-update LR/preclip norm/loss/clipping and terminal status; final checkpoint and resume state hashes; held-out prediction manifests and official score receipts; fitting-cache manifests, arrays and one/eight-rank parity receipt; separate evidence and weights bundles. Record all failed attempts and exclusions. Do not put data, predictions, caches or weights in Git.

11. **Results and trace.** No gates, profiles, fits, scores, cache exports, bundles, student effects, or leaderboard outcomes have been observed. The local change has only source review and the declared static/config checks recorded in `VALIDATION.json`; receiver execution is pending. Append run/result events under the stable H/E IDs to `research/hypotheses.jsonl` and `research/experiments.jsonl`; update the unified idea index with actual PR URL and merge SHA only after they exist. A draft PR or passing source lint does not establish correctness on B300, teacher quality, student transfer or public transfer.

title: [Experiment] Causal Transformer attention recency on B300
body:
# [Experiment] Test causal Transformer attention recency on B300

1. **Status:** implementation and configs; no tests, numerical parity, profiles,
   fitting, export or scores. Clean receipt-bound data and receiver acceptance
   are prerequisites. This is not a ready submission.
2. **Mechanism:** a fixed additive causal distance penalty on existing RoPE
   attention could prioritize recent signals. Compare bias 0 with bias 1 while
   preserving context 1024 and every other setting. Long-lag signal suppression
   is the main competing explanation. This is inspired by, not identical to,
   [ALiBi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12409).
3. **Compute:** eight B300 per independent teacher candidate, no inference-model
   modification for eventual GRU students. Real throughput, memory and transfer
   must be measured, with student fits and teacher caches explicitly additional.
4. **Comparison:** T768×24, 30 epochs, Muon, LR .0003, warmup 5%, batch 1 per
   rank, 1024 context, BF16/BF16x9 scoped Transformer amendment, fixed final
   checkpoint. Configs differ only in bias value; no empirical optimality claim.
5. **Budget:** 2 control + 2 candidate teachers = 4 new fits, on F0/101001 and
   F2/101002. No reused fits. Student transfer requires at least 4 new students
   and four teacher-cache exports, plus profiles and receipt checks.
6. **Validation:** official pooled masked clipped global WP, per-target deltas,
   paired sequence age/coverage and all failed cells. Two fold-seed-confounded
   pairs cannot prove significance. Existing validation and public scores are

title: [Research] Causal teacher–student hypothesis portfolio
body:
# [Research portfolio] Causal teacher–student and long-context hypotheses

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** One proposal-only draft requested for eight
   ideas. [Hypothesis cards](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/research/experiment_drafts/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/HYPOTHESES.md) and [recipe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/research/experiment_drafts/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/recipe.json) distinguish
   teacher, student, connection, representation and objective branches. Base is
   `research-team` at `7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d`; later source
   changes must be explicitly admitted. No new model implementation or launch.
2. **Why it should work.** Fixed teacher mixes may ignore time variation and
   complementary errors; long history and alternate state updates may improve
   teachers; shared-state students may retain diversity more cheaply. These are
   competing hypotheses, not conclusions. Each card names a matched control,
   alternative explanation and adverse observation.
3. **Compute advantage.** B300 compute can prepare diverse causal teachers,
   cross-fitted targets or longer-context models while retaining a small deployable
   student. Teacher fitting, cache export and evaluation are real costs; any
   reused checkpoints must have compatible source and fitting ancestry. No
   universal speedup, scale law or leaderboard gain is assumed.
4. **Comparison.** Each independent candidate has its own matched control,
   two paired seeds and fixed data/source, transforms, optimizer/schedule,
   updates, checkpoint rule and loss scale before admission. Candidate-specific
   parameter values and the exact common parent/config are not implemented or
   frozen here; they are mandatory in the mechanism-specific implementation PR.
   W18 and tiedlead have different epoch/EMA/initializer contracts and must not
   be treated as interchangeable by the historical fbc exporter.
5. **Fitting panel.** Seven cards propose 2 controls + 2 treatments = four new
   fits each. Disagreement weighting has three arms (constant, increased and
   decreased KD weight) × two seeds = six fits. All eight screens would cost
   **34 primary fits**, including teacher-arm fits in cards 5 and 6, plus any
   prerequisite teacher/cross-fit-parent fits and cache construction; none are
   scheduled. For card 6 choose one architecture (Gated DeltaNet or Mamba) and
   for card 8 one robustness objective before admission; testing additional
   variants requires an explicitly expanded fit budget. Reuse is conditional on exact split,
   ancestry, source and recipe identity. Two seeds on one split are not two
   independent folds. Details and potential extra teacher costs are per card.
6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Primary outcome is the official clipped,
   pooled, weighted two-target WP, on the same scored rows for every arm. A
   tentative working effect of +0.0005 WP versus the matched control motivates
   additional work, not a significance or automatic promotion claim. Record both
   seed deltas, t0/t1, component groups, total tried comparisons and uncertainty.
   Full valid and public feedback are development-exposed; conditional component
   bootstrap does not quantify fit variance or restore independent holdout.
7. **Leakage and representativeness.** Whole sequence/component boundaries;
   fit-only statistics and teacher/cache ancestry; no future rows or labels in
   teacher/student inputs, gates, tokenization or prefixes. OOF gating requires
   separately trained source-qualified teachers excluding the gate-fit units.
   Component matching is approximate; anonymous sequence IDs do not prove time.
   Pretrained models are subject to competition restrictions on external data.
8. **Decision.** A consistent practically useful gain with acceptable resource
   cost justifies a separate replication and complete served-candidate study;
   mixed/small gains remain uncertain, and negative results narrow only that
   recipe. An interval crossing zero alone does not close a direction. A stronger
   teacher without student transfer is not itself a ready submission.
9. **How to run.** Not runnable in this PR: missing exact configurations,
   adaptation, teacher/cache provenance, numerical acceptance, B300 profiles,
   receiver ownership and, for serving, Linux CPU access. No command is offered
   as an executable training recipe. Prepare/admit each card separately; do not
   mutate existing jobs or silently substitute artifacts.
10. **Evidence to return.** Code/source/config, split and all teacher/cache
    identities, source-qualified seeds and cells, losses/LR/gradient norms,
    updates, profiles, model and per-target pooled predictions, all paired
    contrasts, failures, plus separate evidence and model archive SHA256s.
    Serving candidates additionally need exact-ZIP parity, reset/causality,
    quality, size, one-vCPU runtime and memory measurements.
11. **Results and trace.** Zero new fits or profiles. Previous exposed PR52/53
    results and related existing drafts are linked in the [README](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/research/experiment_drafts/causal-teacher-student-hypotheses-20261101/README.md).
    The eight H/E ledger entries refer to proposed work, not independent results.
    No promotion, submission or score claim follows from this draft.

title: Bounded multistage ensemble search on eight B300 GPUs
body:
Run and record a bounded four-stage regression search on the existing eight B300s, then test whether the new GRU recipe is limited by batch/update frequency or TBPTT history. The implementation preserves frozen training/scoring sources, bounded owned processes, native train/valid monitoring and reproducible checkpoint handoff.

## Measured outcome

The original wave produced 39 configured-final model artifacts and one partial GALAM. Its full-primary equal-four ensemble scores **0.684699354**, below fixed fresh TL3 **0.692377425**. Auxiliary train-only selection results are distinct from full-primary results; they are not public-score gains.

The separately approved follow-up is complete: **five fresh four-epoch fits plus exact reused A/1301**, five successful Source6 prediction exports and all 17 expected final rows.

| Arm | Batch / TBPTT / accumulation | Seeds | WP of equal-seed predictions |
|---|---|---|---:|
| A | 256 / 256 / 4 | 1301 reused, 1302 fresh | 0.683351603 |
| B | 64 / 256 / 4 | 1301,1302 | 0.683193608 |
| C | 64 / 1024 / 1 | 1301,1302 | 0.683245345 |

B minus A is negative at both matched seeds (-0.000868371/-0.000526670). C minus B is mixed (+0.000681254/-0.000854826). A/B changes batch and update frequency jointly at fixed epochs; B/C matches updates and nominal row windows while changing detach history/accumulation. All six fixed 5%/10% TL3 additions of the new equal-seed GRU means score below TL3.

A separate six-mixture calculation with previously completed full-primary models has best observed **90% TL3 +10% previous LSTM =0.692502063**, delta +0.000124638. This small development-exposed gain is unconfirmed; its posthoc conditional component interval crosses zero. The historical TL3+GALAM0.692496447 was not rescored here, and the tiny numerical difference does not establish superiority.

## Validation and fixed endpoints

Official train/valid boundary: 10,325 fitting train sequences, zero fitting valid, all 1,873 valid sequences /3,528,273 scored rows. Exclude 282 train sequences connected to valid. No random primary folds or chronology inferred from shuffled seq_ix. Normalizers, teachers, initializers and learned weights cannot include primary valid. The inner 8,260/2,065 train-only control is a nonchronological all-after-warmup proxy.

Follow-up endpoints are configured epoch4, strictFP32 Source4 GRU384x2, same optimizer/schedule/input normalization. No validation-selected endpoint substitutes for the fixed final. Composite weights are fixed; the final panel was frozen after early curves, cheap-mixture results and A/1302 native epoch4 were known. This is exposed development evidence, not independent confirmation or significance/public-transfer evidence.

Train graphs use a fixed16-sequence/all-after-warmup diagnostic, whereas primary valid uses the full is_scored mask. Their absolute gap is not an overfitting test.

## Execution, checks and artifacts

Five actual 50-update profiles passed independent engineering review before fitting. Five fresh fits and five scoring child receipts show exit0/no timeout; native terminal and epoch indexes show requested=completed=4. Canonical WP agrees with separately implemented raw-label NumPy arithmetic within1e-10. Ruff/compilation and actual checkpoint loading were checked. An independent reviewer verified source/config/checkpoint/split bindings and interpretation.

All five new configured-final weights are published. Root and independent reviewer rehashed the actual 41.17MB GitHub ZIP and all63 payload files; model hashes match the actual Source6 score records. Prediction arrays remain on the node and were not independently rehashed locally; final scoring did not recompute the full raw validation Parquet SHA (prior transport/footer/selected-label/mask pins are retained). These are research weights; submission ABI/runtime and public/private transfer are not established.

Delivery finished at16:04:40UTC,82.1minutes after the first profile, within the separate four-hour bound. All owned GPU-producing commands exited; existing NIER/MPS were preserved. No successor is queued. Dashboard retains the native qh-* trajectories at http://127.0.0.1:18777/.

# [Submission] Fresh train-only TL3 candidates with CPU export and receiver checks

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Prepare E-TL3C-SUBMISSION-20261029 / H-TL3C-SUBMISSION-20261029 from the completed PR49 endpoints. Fresh weights are still an external dependency. This serves the existing recurrent student lineage; it does not complete the blocked W18 fit.

2. **Why it should work.** The strongest published fresh individual endpoint is tiedlead seed5 (rounded full-valid WP 0.691415). A fixed 0.34 fbc1k + 0.33 tiedlead seed5 + 0.33 tiedlead seed6 mixture may combine complementary errors. Correlated errors or native feature differences may remove the apparent benefit; compare against the same-mode singleton on the same complete sequences. Shapes alone cannot establish native parity.

3. **Compute advantage.** Reuse already trained endpoints without further B300 fitting. Spend CPU export/evaluation work on the actual served callback. Dynamic INT8 is a submission-time alternative to reduce latency; this packet makes no measured speedup or quality claim. The float32 tensor payload is approximately 12.39 MB plus 2.64 MB of native libraries before ZIP overhead, so quantization is not assumed necessary for size.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Singleton tiedlead seed5 versus the fixed three-member mixture in `recipe.json`; every member uses zero-based `model_ep3.pt` after four epochs. Saved tensors already contain the evaluated EMA; do not apply another EMA or choose an epoch from the observed curve. Compare an explicit nonquantized mode with dynamic INT8. The latter also enables fast activations, so measured drift includes both changes. Bind checkpoints, provenance, split, ancestors, tensor schema, native archive and ZIP bytes. The exporter uses saved train-only normalizers.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Zero new scientific fits, three reused selected endpoints and their existing ancestor records. At most four exported candidates (two recipes by two runtime modes). Engineering profile/parity/full-valid callbacks are not training replications. Do not restart W18, GALAM or other jobs.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Use official `global_wp_clip2_v1`, clipping ±2, pooled weighted correlation and `need_prediction & is_scored`. Replay every row, including warmup, across all 1873 valid sequences and 3528273 scored rows for a full grade. A small profile is not a full grade. This is exposed development validation, not fresh private evidence or statistical significance. Pair each blend with its same-mode singleton and INT8 with its same-candidate float32 baseline. Do not infer a public score.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** The pinned split fits 10325 official-train sequences and no valid sequences, with component overlap exclusions; current competition chronology itself remains source-qualified/partly unverified. Check parent and teacher memberships; preserve the legacy consumed-cache provenance limitation. Inspect causal streaming, warmup independence and A-B-A sequence resets. PR49's `encode` resets row-change features at every4000-row evaluation chunk; the historical opaque native implementation may stream continuously. Require boundary parity evidence or explicitly evaluate a distinct streaming candidate. Old TL3 weights are never copied.

8. **Decision-changing result.** A useful fixed-mixture gain is at least 0.0005 WP over the same served singleton, within the measured resource envelope. INT8's predeclared maximum quality sacrifice is 0.0002 WP relative to the same candidate float32 callback. Lesser/no gain favors the simpler singleton; a quality-loss failure calls for float32 or a runtime repair. An unknown runtime/data identity or semantic mismatch cannot establish readiness. Actual CPU compliance, exact size≤20000000bytes and source trace matter independently of quality. Extrapolated runtime needs an official test-size bound and should leave 20% margin; a projection is not a portal timing result.

9. **How to run.** See packet README: pin receiver assets, export on the receiver, build the Python 3.11 Linux CPU image, first run an eight-sequence profile, then score the frozen full-valid candidates in separate offline single-CPU containers. Paths are explicit and outputs create-only. No GPU is needed for native export/scoring; any Torch reference export remains receiver-only. The target machine needs the checkpoint/provenance/ancestor files and the pinned team native runtime. No local test/training or live-job mutation is part of this PR.

2. **Mechanism.** The existing GRU adaptation dispatches its entire network once
   per row. A sequence GRU call, chunk attention, causal convolutions and pointwise
   decoder remove repeated dispatch while preserving the causal graph. Separately,
   per-step BatchNorm EMA emphasizes the training tail; train-only recalibration
   tests whether its saved inference statistics hurt a frozen checkpoint.
   Kernel dispatch and BN mismatch are separate hypotheses, not established causes
   of the complete epoch time or quality plateau.
3. **Compute value.** Measure complete forward/backward/AdamW updates before
   spending on more epochs. The existing inference trace is motivation, not a
   training-speed prediction. BN uses frozen weights and three typical layerwise
   passes over 256 train sequences, then paired full-valid evaluation.
4. **Frozen comparison.** GRU72, raw112, history64, chunk64, B384, AdamW1e-4,
   beta0.9/0.999, WD0.01, clip1, FP32 and TF32/autocast/BF16x9 off. The two
   copied configurations differ only by the explicit block selector. Per-time BN
   reductions never mix timestamps; recurrent/attention/conv state and TBPTT
   boundaries are preserved. Sampled monitoring uses the original step path.
   BN diagnostic uses the step backend and an immutable indexed checkpoint;
   only running means/variances/counters change, with no optimizer or gradient.
5. **Bounded work.** Zero new scientific fits, zero teacher/student fits, zero
   reused fitted controls counted as replications. This is engineering plus a
   frozen-checkpoint diagnostic, not a 4–6-fit scientific screen. Synthetic
   speed comparison: four warmup and twelve measured updates per backend.
   Optional canonical real-data profiles: 25 updates per backend, including
   sampled monitoring. One checkpoint, one fixed calibration seed/subset, one
   original-versus-recalibrated comparison; no automatic sweep or retraining.
6. **Validation.** Receiver checks compare outputs, state, gradients, BN buffers,
   streaming continuation and causal prefixes. Profile receipts bind source,
   configuration and runtime. BN scores pooled `global_wp_clip2_v1` on complete
   official valid, warmup99 and `is_scored`, reporting both targets and deltas.
   Valid is exposed and checkpoints may have been selected there. No pristine
   holdout, seed robustness, significance or public-score forecast is claimed.
7. **Leakage.** BN membership comes only from the original checkpoint-qualified
   train split. No valid examples or labels enter recalibration. Normalizer,
   source, checkpoint/index and split identities are checked. Source separation
   and approximate feature-linked exclusions do not prove calendar chronology.
   Outputs are new artifacts and cannot overwrite or resume the live checkpoint.
8. **Decision.** Numerical acceptance precedes speed measurement. Threefold
   update speedup is a target, not a result; report wall time and memory even if
   slower. Full-epoch benefit requires subsequent measurement. BN delta at least
   0.001 WP motivates a separately frozen checkpoint/seed confirmation; mixed or
   negative results remain evidence about this calibration method and checkpoint.
9. **Run.** README supplies exact receiver commands for acceptance, synthetic
   update timing, canonical real-data profiles and BN recalibration/evaluation.
   Use a separate clean checkout, one explicitly selected free CUDA GPU and fresh
   output directories. Runtime acceptance and memory measurements are pending;
   there is no silent batch, precision or tolerance fallback.
10. **Evidence.** Return source/config/runtime/device identities, numerical errors,
    per-backend timing/memory, original profile receipts, calibration membership,
    original/candidate checkpoint hashes, before/after BN statistics and both
    target scores. Keep checkpoint and evidence archives separate. Failed or
    incomplete receiver runs remain failures, not quality results.
11. **Trace.** Packet README, recipe, static validation and independent source
    review are linked from unified ideas and append-only H/E ledgers. No local
    tests, training, inference, model imports or GPU profiling ran. No active
    worker, recipe, checkpoint, dashboard or launcher was changed.

title: [Experiment] Transformer quality: width versus context on B300
body:
# [Experiment] Improve standalone Transformer quality: width versus context

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Prepared, zero fits; teacher quality, zero student
   fits. H-TRANSFORMER-WIDTH-CONTEXT-20261028 / E-TRANSFORMER-WIDTH-CONTEXT-20261028-R1.
   Depends on draft #47 at `f0d8da40fb545a630e5f042bfcc3b3360784177e`; targets
   `research-team`. The branch includes that dependency until merged. New work is
   the pure-Transformer packet and minimal shared receiver study routing. Ivan's
   preparation packet; actual worker/cell ownership must be claimed on the receiver.
2. **Mechanism.** More hidden capacity may represent interactions the current
   compact teacher misses; more past KV memory may expose longer-lived predictive
   structure. Separate width/context arms distinguish these mechanisms. Alternative
   explanations include undertraining, LR mismatch and extra compute. LR/dropout/WD
   stay frozen because #44 already targets them; its stopped jobs are not resumed.
3. **Compute advantage.** Train the stronger standalone model first; use two seeds
   to avoid promoting one initialization. Reuse canonical code, not a new trainer.
   R4 already proposes1.54B context scaling; this compact source-separated screen
   tests which axis merits more compute. No universal scaling law, CPU suitability
   or public-score forecast. GRU is not a prerequisite for Transformer research.
4. **Frozen comparison.** Baseline768×16/12heads/window1024; wide1024×16/16heads/window1024;
   context768×16/12heads/window4096. All raw112, five epochs, Muon+AdamW1e-4,
   warmup5%, cosinefloor0.1, WD0.01, dropout0, clip1, W2batch128/rank, chunk512,
   accumulation8, efficient attention and compiled blocks. BF16/BF16x9 follows the
   explicit user precision amendment; masters/loss/gradients/state remain FP32.
   No KD/hints. FINAL5 only, `final_only` retention and exact safe-state resume.
   Window is per layer; KV detaches every512 rows and can span weight updates.
   Data/update budget matched, not compute matched. No claim fiveepochs is optimal.
5. **Bounded panel.** Three arms × seeds1001/1002 = six TOTAL fresh Transformer
   fits; no GRU fits and zero reused completed controls. #47 teachers are unrun.
   Baseline adoption into a later KD packet needs explicit ancestry qualification;
   that adapter is not implemented. No automatic combined width+context arm,
   LR sweep,1.5B scale-up or extra seeds. Twelve-update profiles are separate
   disposable engineering work, not scientific replications.
6. **Validation.** One train-only/full-valid component-purged source split, two
   seeds, pooled official clip2 WP with warmup99 and `is_scored`. All six FINAL5
   endpoints, t0/t1, candidate-minus-baseline deltas and conditional centered-component
   bootstrap intervals. Full valid is exposed development data; two seeds and
   conditional intervals do not establish significance or training variance. No
   inner-valid#43-to-full-valid score subtraction or epoch selection.
7. **Leakage/coverage.** Shared #47 producer covers every physical sequence,
   including train528, and excludes all train components touching valid. Missing
   or corrupt groups fail closed. Fit-only normalization, fresh initialization,
   causal raw inputs, sequence resets and exact source/config/data identities.
   Valid features enter overlap detection only; graph linkage is approximate and
   source separation does not prove calendar chronology. Receiver numerical checks
   and actual full-data coverage remain pending.
8. **Decision-changing result.** For either candidate, mean paired gain≥0.001 WP
   with both seeds nonnegative motivates a separately allocated robustness/horizon
   or scale follow-up. Smaller/mixed gains remain uncertain; inspect target tradeoffs
   and cost. Negative FINAL5 results constrain this recipe, not asymptotic model
   capacity. A zero-crossing conditional interval alone is not a direction kill rule.
9. **Run.** [README](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/transformer-width-context-screen/research/experiment_drafts/transformer-width-context-20261028/README.md) has exact receiver commands. Clean reviewed commit,
   provisioned Linux B300 runtime, two free GPUs, fresh external output root:
   prepare → accept → profile → explicit review/admit → fit → evaluate. Commands
   name one cell and reject cache generation for this study. No local tests,
   training, inference or GPU profiles ran; no remote job started. Profiles may
   fail memory admission; there is no silent batch/precision fallback.
10. **Evidence.** Frozen source/config/data/split/study bindings; correctness and
    all six original/reviewed profiles; rank losses/LR/preclip gradients/updates,
    timing/memory, terminal states and weights; full prediction/grade manifests;
    all paired scores/intervals and resource reports. Return failures too, and
    hash evidence and weight archives separately. No data/model payload in Git.
11. **Results/trace.** [Review](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/transformer-width-context-screen/research/experiment_drafts/transformer-width-context-20261028/REVIEW.md), [static receipt](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/transformer-width-context-screen/research/experiment_drafts/transformer-width-context-20261028/VALIDATION.json), unified
    index and append-only H/E records accompany the runnable packet. Zero quality
    measurements for this study. Publication does not resume jobs, merge PRs or
    establish hardware readiness. Compression can later compare student families;
    it is not the current research focus.

Incremental changes after dependency #47: [review this study only](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/compare/f0d8da40fb545a630e5f042bfcc3b3360784177e...codex/transformer-width-context-screen).

title: [Experiment] Source-separated Transformer to GRU distillation on B300
body:
# [Experiment] Source-separated compact Transformer to GRU distillation

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Implementation handoff, not a result or a launch.
   H-SOURCE-HOLDOUT-TRANSFORMER-KD-20261028 /
   E-SOURCE-HOLDOUT-TRANSFORMER-KD-20261028-R1; connection/teacher/student experiment.
   Based on `research-team` at `7e4074314a62d0907c9608f9220cf72958708a2d`, including
   the merged #32/#42 canonical trainer. The preparation owner is Ivan's research
   packet; a receiving B300 worker must claim the actual cells before launching.
   Adds a full-source split producer/loader, six complete configurations, explicit
   profile/admission/fit/cache/evaluation commands and a paired results report.
   Local tests, model imports, training, inference and GPU profiles were not run.

2. **Why it should work.** #43 establishes that a compact causal Transformer can
   learn the task, but its component-held-out development protocol fitted some
   official valid-source rows. It does not answer whether its predictions help a
   fresh GRU when all official valid data are excluded from fitting. A same-seed
   teacher may suppress noisy label variation while transferring temporal
   structure. The decisive comparison is KD versus an otherwise identical
   labels-only GRU. Both use the same initialization seed, training membership,
   normalization, update schedule and loss scale. A normalized label/teacher WMSE
   removes the trivial doubled-gradient-scale explanation; teacher errors,
   capacity limits and training-target overfitting remain alternative explanations.
   Teacher predictions on fitting rows are in-sample; this is not out-of-fold KD.

3. **Compute advantage.** Two fresh Transformer fits buy new training-only
   teachers; four GRU fits measure whether their benefit survives compression.
   This answers a deployment-relevant question before funding another 1.54B
   ladder. More GPU memory permits the existing compiled causal context1024
   teacher; more compute does not establish a scaling law. The GRU is a future
   CPU candidate, with package size, latency and quantization deliberately left
   to a later measured submission phase. No serving or leaderboard gain is claimed.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Raw112 inputs, full eligible train-source data,
   all valid-source sequences evaluated, five fixed epochs, no early stopping or
   full-valid checkpoint selection. Whole graph components touching valid are
   excluded from train. Fit-only normalization, official scoring mask with first99
   rows excluded, causal inputs and sequence-state reset are shared. Teacher:
   Transformer768×16, 12heads, FF4, context1024, dropout0, efficient attention,
   compiled blocks, Muon+AdamW LR1e-4, batch128/rank. Students: GRU256×2,
   AdamW LR1e-3, batch32/rank. All use W2, chunk512, accumulation8, warmup5%,
   cosine floor0.1, weight decay0.01, clip1. Explicit BF16/BF16x9 follows the
   user-approved precision amendment; weights/gradients/loss/optimizer state are
   FP32, and this is not strict IEEE-FP32 compute. Labels-only has KD weight0;
   KD has weight1 and `(WMSE_label + WMSE_teacher)/2`. Optional normalization
   preserves legacy additive behavior/config hashes when omitted. Only the fixed
   final epoch5 becomes the scientific endpoint. Retention is `final_only`, with
   resumable safe state. Exact settings are in the six committed JSON configs.
   Teacher versus GRU compares useful recipes, not isolated architecture at equal
   compute. Batches are candidates until newly profiled on the receiver.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Six TOTAL new scientific fits: two teachers, two
   labels-only GRUs and two KD GRUs at seeds1001/1002. This is one split and two
   seeds, not two folds. Zero reused controls. #43 checkpoints have invalid
   ancestry for this protocol; #46's event211 GRU, optimizer and adaptive horizon
   are not an exact control. Their published metrics are context only. Each cell
   first requires a disposable 12-update engineering profile and explicit review;
   profiles are not scientific replications or permission to change batch/LR.
   No automatic queue, retries, extra seeds or scale sweep.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Fixed final endpoints are evaluated once on
   all valid-source sequences with canonical pooled `global_wp_clip2_v1`, including
   t0/t1, selected-row and component counts. Report all six endpoints and each
   seed's teacher-minus-labels and KD-minus-labels differences. Equal-weight seed
   means summarize the panel; two seeds cannot establish significance, independent
   fold robustness or training-variance coverage. Official valid has already been
   exposed to team development. It is source-separated from these new fits, not
   pristine confirmation. No comparison against #43's differently selected
   inner-valid scores is interpreted as a gain/loss. Source files do not prove
   chronological ordering; `seq_ix` is an identifier, not a verified timestamp.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** A new feature-only graph and thin source-qualified
   indexes cover every physical row group, including train528. Legacy graph caches
   silently omit that group and are not reused. Missing/corrupt data fail preparation;
   there is no automatic exclusion. Every train component linked to any valid
   component is purged; no valid rows enter loss, normalizer, initialization or KD
   cache. Valid features are used only for graph-based overlap exclusion, which
   is a transductive preprocessing choice. Approximate feature-derived components
   are not proof against every unknown duplicate or temporal linkage. Exact
   data/index/graph/split identities are recorded. Teacher caches cover only fit
   members and must match the designated same-seed fresh teacher, source, config
   and terminal epoch5 checkpoint. No old checkpoint, ensemble or foreign cache
   substitution is accepted. Receiver causal-prefix and data checks remain pending.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Predeclared follow-up signal: mean KD-minus-labels
   WP at least +0.001 and nonnegative on both seeds, with no invalid/nonfinite
   endpoints. This justifies a separately allocated robustness/serving study, not
   a submission or significance claim. Mixed signs, target disagreement or a smaller
   positive gain are uncertain and require inspecting all cells and cost. Negative
   results narrow this five-epoch single-teacher recipe, not all Transformer/KD
   directions. A weak standalone teacher suggests improving teacher learning before
   scaling distillation. No confidence-interval sign alone closes the direction.

9. **How to run.** See the packet [README](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/source-holdout-transformer-kd/research/experiment_drafts/source-holdout-transformer-kd-20261028/README.md), `receiver.env.example` and
   `run.sh`. Use a clean checkout at a full pinned commit in an already provisioned
   Linux B300 runtime. Prepare complete source caches/split first. Choose exactly
   two free GPUs, profile one explicit cell, review its receipt, admit, then fit.
   Export each fixed-final teacher's fit-only cache before profiling that seed's
   KD student. Evaluate fixed endpoints after fitting; compare only when all six
   complete. Fresh roots and exact identity checks protect existing jobs/artifacts.
   All actual environment/data/numerical acceptance and profiles are pending.

10. **Evidence to return.** Exact Git/source/config/environment/data/split hashes,
    prepared-source membership/exclusions, six original/reviewed profiles, run
    provenance, losses, LR, preclip gradient norms, attempted/successful updates,
    nonfinite events, elapsed time and memory, terminal statuses, final checkpoint
    hashes, teacher cache manifests, prediction manifests, canonical grades and
    the complete paired comparison. Return failures and exclusions too. Archive
    compact receipts/logs separately from weights/cache arrays, with hashes and
    storage locations; do not upload private data or model payloads to Git.

11. **Results and trace.** Six fits remain unrun. No quality, throughput, hardware
    fit or CPU-submission result exists for this packet. See [static validation](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/source-holdout-transformer-kd/research/experiment_drafts/source-holdout-transformer-kd-20261028/VALIDATION.json),
    [independent review](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/source-holdout-transformer-kd/research/experiment_drafts/source-holdout-transformer-kd-20261028/REVIEW.md), [unified ideas](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/codex/source-holdout-transformer-kd/research/unified/ideas/README.md),
    and append-only H/E ledger entries. Publication and merge are distinct from
    source-bound run evidence. The draft PR URL and published commit are recorded
    on publication; receiver results must reference the actual training commit.

title: [Experiment] Eight-L4 GRU/GALAM quality runs with chronological validation
body:
# Fixed eight-L4 quality panel with full chronological validation

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Exactly eight fresh full fits were launched on
eight L4s under launch `e635250b62fa489d94c987d4898ff417`; plain GRU is terminal and
seven GALAM continue unchanged. The approved panel is in
`launch/PANEL.json`; complete sources and all eight actual-source profiles passed
independent resource/identity review. Root owns delivery through results. GALAM
is reconstructed from Denis Tomin's screenshots with explicit unknown original
dimensions; no exact reproduction claim is made.
2. **Why it should work.** Test capacity, recurrent depth/type, attention history,
gradient horizon and matrix optimization against the full schematic GALAM
LSTM64 control. Plain GRU256x2/event211 is a historical whole-system benchmark,
not a pure recurrent-cell ablation. Each GALAM arm changes only its declared
treatment; dimensions needed by a wider/GRU model are part of that treatment.
3. **Compute advantage.** Eight independent L4s give one lane per fixed arm.
Strict-FP32 synthetic sweeps and eight successful full-input real profiles govern
the frozen GRU32/GALAM384 batches, one-batch prefetch and eval384 setting.
Memory occupancy is not evidence of delivered training speed or quality.
4. **Frozen comparison.** GPU0: plain GRU256x2/211 causal features/gate-wise Muon
plus AdamW/LR1e-3. GPU1: GALAM LSTM64/AdamW/LR1e-4. GPUs2–7: width128, depth2,
GRU72, history256, TBPTT256, attention/FFN-only Muon respectively. Common seed1001,
strict FP32, fresh weights, no teacher/KD/old initializer, weight decay.01,
clip1, maximum20epochs, warmup-cosine-v2 with5% warmup, train-only all-fit moments.
AdamW beta1.9/beta2.999/eps1e-8; Muon momentum.95/NS5/eps1e-7. Common GALAM batch384
is frozen and hashed; plain GRU keeps32. No LR scaling was added.
5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Exactly8 new scientific fits, one per GPU; no reused
trained control, additional seed, teacher or distillation fits. Engineering
profiles discard their weights. Stop policy: min5 completed epochs,
patience4, min_delta.0005; hard maximum20. Keep every epoch and best/last pointers.
6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Official earlier train fits; complete official
later valid reports original is_scored mask and pooled global_wp_clip2_v1 plus
t0/t1 each epoch. Train-eval32 sequences use explicitly labelled all-after-warmup
rows. Best/stop selection exposes valid; this single-seed screen cannot estimate
training variance or establish significance/private transfer.
7. **Leakage and coverage.** No random primary folds or chronology inferred from
seq_ix. Pin full sources, preserve whole sequences, exclude train components
connected to valid, audit complete source coverage including train group528.
Fit normalization and all ancestry only on retained train members. The adopted
Predictorium chronology is user policy; current calendar timestamps are unproven.
8. **Decision-changing result.** Compare full-valid best/last curves, per-target
deltas and cost to the matched GALAM control. Improvement supports follow-up;
negative or inconclusive single-seed results do not prove a direction useless.
Plain GRU compares the complete system, not an isolated architecture component.
9. **How to run.** The active isolated Torch2.8+cu128 runtime on the authorized
eight-L4 host. `launch/prepare_data.py` audits/indexes/builds the chronological
manifest and prewarmed raw112/event211 normalization on10325 retained train
sequences. Full valid keeps1873 sequences;282 train sequences connected to valid
are excluded. Eight exact-source profiles exercised diagnostics and a prefetched
successor. `scripts/launch_galam_quality8.py` admitted reviewed identity-matched
receipts and started detached owned workers with GPU/CPU affinity. The read-only
dashboard is on loopback18766; node hourly/terminal GitHub reporting survives SSH.
Do not duplicate the active panel. Foreign services are untouched.
10. **Evidence to return.** Config/source/data/runtime hashes, ownership/PIDs,
train/valid loss and WP/t0/t1 curves, LR/preclip gradient norm, sampled model and
CPU/RAM/VRAM/disk telemetry, elapsed/work counts, all epoch checkpoints and
strict-best/last pointers. Keep large payloads on approved storage; publish
bounded evidence and results with honest completion percentages.
11. **Results and trace.** Plain GRU stopped after10epochs under its declared
policy; best epoch8 full-valid WP0.677856123. Seven original GALAM fits continue
with their original PID/starttick/source/config bindings. Frozen GALAM-LSTM128
epoch3 scores0.672369413 and GALAM-GRU72 epoch3 scores0.671357523 alone.

A separately frozen inference-only diagnostic on the freedGPU0 reproduced all
three standalone scores on1873official-valid sequences/3528273scored rows.
Primary fixed80%GRU+20%GALAM-LSTM128 scores **0.681219679**, delta **+.003363555**;
with GALAM-GRU72 it scores **0.680993482**, delta **+.003137359**. Both targets
improve. A separate review session independently rescored actual hashed
LSTM128/GRU arrays with a float64 formula, agreeing within2e-13. Fixed10/30%
sensitivities are reported beside predeclared20%primary; no coefficients fitted.

These are exposed, single-seed results against the clean GRU benchmark, not the
full deployed team ensemble, hidden transfer or CPU package approval. Zero new
scientific fits; the diagnostic worker exited and freedGPU0. An independent
source/log audit identifies an untested BN running-stat risk. Actual short
inference traces show high per-time kernel-launch counts; no backward/optimizer
profiling claim is made.

Results, independent rescore, complete fixed panel, prediction/trace hashes,
timing and original-fit continuity:
`research/experiment_drafts/galam-ensemble-diagnostics-20261028/RESULTS.md`.

title: R5: B300 launch commands and post-selection checkpoint retention
body:
# R5 B300 launch handoff and post-selection checkpoint retention

Keeping 30 FP32 snapshots for all four 1.54B fits would occupy roughly 740 GB
before optimizer states or predictions. This follow-up to merged #42 runs one
LR pair through both complete epoch curves and the frozen shared-epoch selector,
exports MIDAS evidence, and provides an explicit hash-bound cleanup action before
the next pair. Selected weights, fixed-final weights, resume state and evidence
are retained. No experiment result or B300 readiness is claimed.

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Engineering preparation for
   H/E-B300-TRANSFORMER-RECOVERY-R5, based on research-team merge `7e407431`.
   Teacher execution/retention only; receiver owns admission and execution.
2. **Mechanism.** Reduce simultaneous stored snapshots by finishing and archiving
   one LR pair before the next. This changes storage order, not model quality.
   Keeping per-fold best alone is insufficient for a shared mean-WP winner.
3. **Compute advantage.** Existing eight-B300 fits and full inner sweeps remain.
   Hash verification adds disk I/O. Weight-only peak estimate is ~407 GB, with

title: Research evidence: missing controls, batch weighting and quota packages
body:
# October 24 research evidence: missing controls, batch weighting and quota packages

Recovered predictions show that the apparent online-correction gain is shared with the history-aware control and does not reproduce on the second fold/seed. A clip-aware decomposition narrows simple calibration as the explanation; a separate full fitting-cache scan exposes substantial batch reweighting. This draft preserves those findings, the requested Astra reframing, all-PR inspection, live EDA and two technically checked exploratory submission ZIP identities.

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Root-owned completed artifact grades and diagnostics, with independent bounded source/result reviews. Main lineage is H-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1; new records cover F0/F1 shrink, fixed direction geometry, fit batch mass and TL3/H390 quota replacements. The historical twelve-fit panel remains incomplete. Source execution was on `c3e208b387ead0ec967f9abc4b14275eb8ba94c5` plus the preserved source delta; this evidence PR is based on research-team and does not claim that all its runtime sources are identical.

2. **Why it should work.** The question is whether the extra relationship state adds information beyond generic head capacity, existing event inputs and the mean-only arm. A already retains history/adaptation. The missing equal-capacity zero-state control is a discriminating follow-up. Calibration variance overlap must not be confused with score contribution. Batch normalization is another concrete variable, with beneficial component balancing as an alternative explanation.

3. **Compute advantage.** Existing predictions and compact five-column fit suffixes answer these questions without another teacher or recurrent fit. The direction pass takes 90.434 seconds and the batch scan 6.942 seconds on one local CPU. Large-teacher/B300 progress is reported separately, with no paid compute or invented scaling/leaderboard forecast. Cache reconstruction remains a delivery bottleneck, so no uncosted full route is admitted.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Each linked packet preserves exact source, recipe, ancestry, membership and input hashes. The official `global_wp_clip2_v1` remains unchanged. Shrink uses an additional fixed float32 alpha 0.1; the direction probe uses real-arithmetic clipped right derivatives and target-specific weights. The batch audit follows 8,192 ordered rows, both targets, the original row weights and 1e-8 denominator clamp. Quota packages retain TL3’s two teachers and use H390 S3 at 0.34 or S3/S4 at 0.17 each, frozen before the new sample grade.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Actual new scientific fits: **zero**. New teacher, student and recurrent fitting costs: **zero**. Saved F0/F1 heads/parents and all-data H390S3/S4 are reused with exact provenance limitations. The proposed next Z-versus-A screen is **four total small-head fits**, two arms across F0/seed2201 and F1/seed2202, subject to unused-seed/provenance and complete-cost checks; it is not admitted here. No historical panel is silently changed. Kaggle version4’s engineering-update count is unknown after timeout, not asserted to be zero.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** F0 uses 468 groups / 141 components; F1 uses 457 groups / 149 components. Fixed A shrink gives+0.000131368WP/F0 and−0.000004696/F1. B/C derivative residuals after calibration+commonA are mixed with conditional intervals crossing zero; this is not an equivalence result. The quota sample uses 32 components per F0/F2 stratum; pair-vs-TL3 deltas are+.003742/+.000205. These are fitted diagnostics because H390 used train+valid and retained TL3 ancestry is unknown. Direction point/projection checks passed independently; independent numerical bootstrap reconstruction remained incomplete and is disclosed. No clean holdout, reliable training-variance estimate or public-score increment is claimed.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Existing folds were repeatedly exposed. Source-qualified groups, dependency components, teacher/initializer ancestry and prior target access are recorded. The no-fit direction analysis uses evaluation-label-weighted projections only descriptively and exports no coefficients. The batch audit reads fitting labels only. Exact native quota callbacks pass sequence reset and finite-output checks on the frozen full-sequence sample, with selected local ISA execution rather than universal-platform claims.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Prioritize the missing equal-capacity state control before spending on more relationship complexity. Preserve the uncertain C-lag1 residual as a possible follow-up; a zero-crossing interval is not an automatic kill rule. Treat batch normalization as a measurable intervention, not proof of a wrong loss family. Keep failed cache delivery separate from scientific negative evidence. Use the S3/S4 quota package first under the user’s exploratory request, with public transfer still unknown.

9. **How to run.** This PR preserves completed evidence and grants no new execution. Exact worker commands, dependency/source identities, private cache locations and output paths are in the linked execution receipts and packet READMEs. Historical local runs use one CPU, explicit 400,000,000-byte worker limits, physical scratch, no swap and the 1 GiB aggregate cap. The source snapshot explains how the execution base differs from this integration branch. Kaggle version4 terminated without a usable profile; GPU/full-fit candidates remain unadmitted and missing measured end-to-end feasibility is explicit.

10. **Evidence to return.** Included: recipes/manifests, source and real-producer fixtures, terminal logs/receipts, result JSON, independent reviews, all-PR source/artifact inventories, marimo notebook and ten figure families. Private payload identities/access locations remain in manifests: exact ZIPs, predictions, derived component moments, targets and remote engineering archives. No model-training progress or new checkpoints are invented when there were no scientific fits.

11. **Results and trace.** Start at the [campaign synthesis](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/resume4h-evidence-20261024/research/campaign_2026-10-24/resume4h_r1/CAMPAIGN_SYNTHESIS_R1.md), [Astra fundamentals](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/resume4h-evidence-20261024/research/campaign_2026-10-24/resume4h_r1/astra_fundamentals_r1/README.md), [direction result](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/resume4h-evidence-20261024/research/campaign_2026-10-24/resume4h_r1/feasibility_scout/direction_probe_r1/RESULTS_R2.md), [batch audit](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/resume4h-evidence-20261024/research/campaign_2026-10-24/resume4h_r1/feasibility_scout/batch_mass_audit_r1/RESULTS_R1.md), and [quota handoff](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/resume4h-evidence-20261024/research/campaign_2026-10-24/resume4h_r1/quota_submission_r1/RESULTS_AND_HANDOFF_R1.md).
