title: [Experiment] TL3 student: labels vs clean-fold distillation
body:
# [Experiment] E-TL3-CLEAN-KD-20261023-R1: paired TL3 student labels versus clean teacher distillation

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Implemented, unrun; preparation owned by Ivan Vorfolomeev, GPU receiver/operator unassigned. Student/teacher connection experiment H-TL3-CLEAN-KD-20261023 → E-TL3-CLEAN-KD-20261023-R1. Base `research-team` at `b4365e01adef57f4a5c9313faecf26952f0f5287`. Extends the canonical trainer with a causal tiedlead encoder and prepares a bounded receiver, source/data binding, teacher-cache export, independent fit audit, complete-mixture grader and evidence bundles. Zero completed fits, GPU profiles or measured gain. Local tests, inference and training were explicitly forbidden and were not run.

2. **Why it should work.** An ensemble target may reduce idiosyncratic label noise and transfer book/event structure into the smaller plain TL3 student. Predicted observation: KD improves the student's official score and its marginal contribution to the fixed mixture. Alternative: any historical gain came from warm ancestry, auxiliary heads or a different teacher family; or fresh teachers/students underfit. The labels-only arm uses identical caches, fitting pool, loss code, initialization, normalization and sample order, differing only in alpha 0 versus 0.5. [Hinton et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531) motivates ensemble-to-student transfer, not a forecast for this task.

3. **Compute advantage.** Two new tiedlead teachers per fold receive four full epochs; students receive two. Extra B300 compute buys independent teacher fits and their two-seed average without admitting unverifiable production ancestry. The student remains the 211-input H256×2 GELU-head GRU architecture. Teacher GPU cost is explicit and can be amortized over later separately approved transfer experiments. No scaling law, latency, occupancy or public-score improvement is claimed before measurement. A positive student result still needs separate one-CPU inference/size admission before a submission.

4. **Frozen comparison.** F0/1001 and F2/1002 students, cold and paired. Each fold's two teachers are cold, label-only, 263-input tiedlead H256×2. Complete eligible train+valid component pools, fitting-only canonical normalization, deterministic seeded batches, strict FP32, no autocast/TF32/quantization. AdamW LR .001/WD .01, OneCycle, batch32, chunk/update/detach2000, full20000-row sequences, clip1. Per-window canonical WMSE uses clipped-label absolute weights; KD target is .5 clipped labels + .5 clipped mean of two teachers. No auxiliary targets, future-label bootstrap or propensity. Four teacher epochs/fixed ep3; two student epochs/fixed ep1. No fit-time outer evaluation or checkpoint selection. State resets at sequence boundaries; encoder book deltas explicitly carry across chunks. This repairs the archived boundary reset, so historical numerical parity is not claimed. Explicit epoch-state resume preserves source/runtime/optimizer/sampler/RNG contract and original cold-start receipt.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** **8 new scientific fits:** F0 teachers2001/2002 + labels1001 + KD1001; F2 teachers2003/2004 + labels1002 + KD1002. Four teacher prerequisites, two control students, two KD students, zero reused fits. This dated panel explicitly amends the usual 4–6 initial-fit screen: two teachers on two clean folds need four prerequisite fits because production ancestry is uncertified. Six short engineering profiles are separate and are not scientific replications. No search, coefficient tuning, automatic retries or expansion. No remote allocation or fit is started by this PR.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Primary: equal-cell mean KD-minus-labels official `global_wp_clip2_v1` for the complete endpoints, each `.34*student + .33*teacher_a + .33*teacher_b`. Also return standalone students, teacher-only average, full-mixture deltas versus teacher-only, t0/t1, component counts and every cell. Official mask and complete outer-valid membership; no sparse subset scored as a full fold. Paired whole-component bootstrap:10,000, seed231023. Intervals condition on fixed fits; two fold/seed cells cannot estimate training-seed variance, prove significance or remove development exposure. No best-seed selection.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** F0/F2 split hashes are frozen in `recipe.json`; the canonical splitter recomputes feature-only connected components and excludes them across sources. No production initializer, teacher/cache, propensity or auxiliary learned feature. Teacher cache exports use fitting features only, exact source-qualified ordering and zero padding outside fitting groups; checkpoint/source/sidecar hashes and FP32 provenance are checked on both creation and reuse. New lead features only gather from the current/past sequence prefix. These folds are exposed development evidence; ancestry exclusion is not a pristine or proven future-regime holdout. Dataset anonymity and residual cross-component dependence limit representativeness claims.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Both complete-mixture cell deltas nonnegative and mean ≥+.0003 justify a separately budgeted confirmation, not a submission claim. Mixed signs or a zero-crossing interval remain uncertain. Negative complete-mixture results constrain this exact alpha/teacher/budget recipe, with standalone and teacher-only results distinguishing weak teachers, student underfitting and ensemble redundancy. Never add a local delta to a leaderboard score. No adaptive teacher/mixture/checkpoint selection after seeing outcomes.

9. **How to run.** Follow [the packet README](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/tl3-clean-fold-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/tl3-clean-fold-distillation/README.md). On an allocated Linux B300 receiver: `uv sync --frozen --group research --group dev`, activate `.venv`, set `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src:$PWD`; fill external absolute data/split/portable-registry paths, then `receiver.py bind` and `preflight`. Run the prepared causal/chunk tests there. Assign one B300 per cell, then `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 WNN_TL3_ASSETS=/physical/scratch/tl3-bound.json bash research/experiment_drafts/tl3-clean-fold-distillation/run_cell.sh F0`; use another assigned device for F2. Run `receiver.py score` and `bundle` after both complete. Failed profiles stop admission; failed fits preserve logs and support only explicit full epoch-state resume. A failure before the first saved epoch needs a separately reviewed restart. Source/data bindings, actual B300 profiles and receiver tests remain pending.

10. **Evidence to return.** Bound source/recipe/assets/runtime and GPU UUID; every profile, start/terminal/audit receipt; all canonical losses, learning rates, preclip gradient/step diagnostics, sample order, normalization, epoch provenance, elapsed time and peak/reserved memory; exact held-out prediction sidecars/arrays; all scores/conditional intervals and decision status. `bundles/evidence.tar.gz` and `bundles/weights.tar.gz` remain separate with SHA256 manifest; no raw datasets or portal upload. Storage is the mounted project's `research_tmp/tl3-clean-kd-r1`, plus canonical `artifacts/runs` and `cache` paths. Receipts retain failed/resumed attempts.

11. **Results and trace.** No scores or archives exist yet. Source-level independent criticism found and resolved: historical TL3 student and served tiedlead members have different uncertified ancestry; cache reuse needed the same FP32/scope checks as fresh export; existing completed roles must be revalidated/skipped; the objective is chunk-normalized; tiedlead must omit independent-width flags; resume probes see restored tensors and must preserve the original initial-state identity separately. [Unified ideas index](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/tl3-clean-fold-distillation/research/unified/ideas/README.md) and append-only H/E ledgers point to this packet. Published head/PR identity is verified after creation; merge and B300 results are pending.

title: Online input relationships with a frozen-parent residual head
body:
# Online input relationships with a frozen-parent residual head

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** The implemented screen H-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1 / E-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1 is incomplete at its original worker time cap. The worker ended at 03:10:32 Kyiv on October23 with timeout/SIGTERM after 7,800.451 service seconds. Seven of twelve heads are saved: all six F0 heads and F1/lag1/A. F1/lag1/B stopped after epochs0–1 without a durable checkpoint; four heads never started. Both parent caches remain on approved physical scratch. No quality grading or retry ran. The proposed one-hour allocation transfer remains unanswered and unapproved; the 12-hour production reserve is untouched. [Terminal evidence](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/5ce677916ce028bdafe75bebea0cc14c997e71cf/research/experiment_drafts/online-relationships-20261022/PANEL_TERMINAL_R1.json) and [independent metadata review](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/5ce677916ce028bdafe75bebea0cc14c997e71cf/research/experiment_drafts/online-relationships-20261022/TERMINAL_METADATA_REVIEW_R1.json) record the outcome. Root owns delivery and the independent grader owns validation/scoring. The executed source freeze is `17470a770f2a6aa25be232c017bff45b5d56ad97`; reproducible recipe/admission/launcher packet is root `33c6e33830a89187aaaf08116850864250feed56`. This focused PR is not the executed checkout: four preserved canonical dependency files differ from the frozen run hashes, so its exact source preflight rejects PR HEAD. No PR-branch parity or quality claim is made.

2. **Why it should work.** A causal state of input-only forecasts, pre-update innovations and slopes may reveal residual structure that the frozen parent misses. Arm A adapts the mean only and fixes slope to zero; B adapts slope/intercept through row 98, then freezes; C continues updating slope/intercept. C−A asks whether relationships add value beyond mean adaptation; C−B asks whether continued adaptation helps after warmup. A lower input-prediction loss alone is not evidence of endpoint value. The strongest alternatives are ordinary calibration, fold/seed variation and a learned residual distribution that does not transfer from in-sample parent predictions.

3. **Compute advantage and measured limit.** A 64-unit tanh residual readout reuses each frozen parent; there are no new GRU or teacher fits. The original inclusive gate projected 8,311.440 seconds within the 9,000-second panel ceiling. During delivery, CPU-package heat required lowering the worker from 190% to 100% CPU. The unchanged 7,800-second service cap then ended delivery before the complete panel. The actual service elapsed was 7,800.451 seconds including shutdown; this is a delivery-cost result, not evidence of predictive value. B300 stays deferred, and no production time is borrowed. Any continuation requires the pending allocation decision and fresh bounded recovery admission, retaining completed outputs and charging the interrupted head's refit.

4. **Frozen comparison.** The admitted immutable recipe uses 419 inputs: canonical `standard211` plus matured i0 changes, forecasts, pre-update errors and slopes (52 each). The online state uses raw observations only, updates causally, resets at each sequence, and never reads labels, scoring masks or prediction flags. Separate lag-1 and lag-16 panels are used. The residual is `parent + 0.1 * head`; head output initializes to zero. All arms use strict FP32 with autocast and TF32 off; canonical fitting row weights and WMSE; AdamW at 0.001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clip 1, batches of 8,192 rows, three epochs and fixed epoch-2 checkpoint selection. Fit-only standardization uses a 0.001 standard-deviation floor and clips standardized differences to ±8. Means/covariance start at zero, input variance at one; slope ridge is 0.1 and the state half-life is 512. The exact optimizer, target, parent, sequence and reset contracts are pinned in `EXECUTION_RECIPE_R1.json` and `PANEL_ADMISSION_R1.json`.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** The explicit lag amendment admits two matched panels: folds 0 and 1 with readout fitting seeds 1001 and 1002, respectively (the two reused parents have their own pinned seed-3 ancestry); each cell has arms A/B/C at lags 1 and 16. This is 4 new readout fits per arm, 2 per arm per lag, and 12 total new fits. Two exact fold-specific parent endpoints are reused across the arms/lags. There are zero new GRU fits, teacher fits or backbone/student fits. Each cell uses the recipe-pinned 10% source-qualified component sample and complete sequences. No additional follow-up fits are included in this admission.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** The unchanged official metric is `global_wp_clip2_v1`, with its fixed scored/prediction mask, ±2 clipping and original clipped-label magnitude weights. The grader evaluates both targets and four fixed position bins on both source-qualified folds. Planned primary contrasts are C−A, C−B and each arm against its matched parent within each fold/lag; lag-16 minus lag-1 per arm/cell is secondary (26 contrasts total). The paired dependency-component bootstrap is conditional on these fixed endpoints and excludes fitting variation and public transfer. Both folds are exposed; the two fold/seed cells confound those axes and cannot estimate training variance or establish significance. Report every paired delta and interval; do not promote on an isolated positive component interval.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Online updates are past-only and use raw inputs, not targets, masks or request/score flags. Unavailable backward differences are zero placeholders and excluded from fitting standardization until mature; warmup spans rows 16–98, with 82 real lag-1 and 67 real lag-16 regressor pairs. Sequence state resets on boundaries. Exact cache headers, source-qualified membership, parent normalization and coverage are checked before grading. Parent training predictions are in-sample rather than OOF, so the learned residual distribution may differ on held-out components. All folds used here are exposed; this screen does not create a fresh holdout.

8. **Decision-changing result.** A coherent endpoint improvement for C over A and B supports continued relationship adaptation in this readout; improvement only over A is consistent with calibration rather than ongoing adaptation. An input-loss improvement without official endpoint value earns no expansion. The screen is small, so mixed or imprecise results remain uncertain and can justify only a bounded information-seeking follow-up when its expected value exceeds its cost. Negative evidence narrows this exact readout and panel; it does not reject online learning generally. B has only 83 matured warmup outcomes, with 82/67 real lag-1/lag-16 regressors; C−B cannot establish nonstationarity. title: [Experiment] Cold-label GRU NLL vs WMSE: four fits, three epochs
body:
# [Experiment] Cold-label mean/logvariance NLL on full GRU

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Prepared draft, not launched; zero GPU jobs and zero new scores. Branch: `experiment/b300-nll-labels-20261022`, based on `68ff682977b822f38351aac0f621146f5f13b440`, the source child used by the prior warm NLL result. This is a NEW cold-label objective adaptation, not a faithful replication of the warm MainT3 experiment. H/E IDs and owner remain to be assigned by the coordinating campaign. No parent checkpoint, teacher, cache, or learned preprocessing artifact is used.

2. **Why it should work.** A clipped-label weighted Gaussian NLL may learn useful scale-dependent errors while retaining the same mean outputs and score-facing predictions as WMSE. The new path uses the observed clipped labels, `w = abs(clipped_label) * main_valid`, and `w * (exp(-clamp(logvar,-4,4)) * (mean-target)^2 + clamp(logvar,-4,4))`, divided by `max(sum(w), 1e-8)`. The strongest alternative is that label noise makes variance fitting distract the shared representation; the matched WMSE arm distinguishes objective value from model size and initialization.

   Existing evidence is mixed and narrow. A prior warm/teacher NLL fit completed six epochs without nonfinite updates, establishing stability only. Its first exposed F0/seed1001 paired endpoint was +0.000738 WP versus WMSE, with a component-paired 95% interval of [-0.000293, +0.001870], crossing zero. That NLL arm used a warm H256x2 parent and a 0.9 MainT3 teacher blend. It does not establish the effect of cold, labels-only NLL. The source-qualified result receipt is in the coordinating checkout at `research/campaign_2026-10-19/full_gru_tweaks_r1`; it is not vendored here.

3. **Compute advantage.** The test changes the training objective without introducing teacher generation or cache preparation. It uses a three-epoch fixed endpoint and four total science fits across two matched cells. Each independent fit is single-GPU in the current trainer. This source has no DDP path, so this NLL cohort cannot use all eight B300s concurrently; the coordinating operator may schedule other authorized comparisons on the remaining devices. Do not duplicate fits merely to occupy GPUs.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Two arms per cell: (A) WMSE and (B) labels-only NLL. Both set `--mean-variance-head 1`, so the final layer has the same shape and zero-initialized two-row log-variance append. Paired arms use the same fresh seed and otherwise identical recipe. Proposed cells are F0/seed1201 and F2/seed1202. Each fit uses the complete source-qualified fitting membership in its frozen outer-fold manifest, no subset, and never trains on that fold's excluded evaluation components. Use the plain 2-layer H256 GRU, linear encoder, full source sequence context, batch32, chunk2000, AdamW at LR0.001, weight decay0.01, beta2=0.999, OneCycle schedule, global gradient clip1.0, three epochs, and fixed zero-based checkpoint epoch2. Strict FP32 applies to parameters, recurrent state, activations, gradients and floating optimizer state; disable autocast and TF32 and require highest FP32 matmul precision. Both arms fit their own normalization from identical fitting membership. Labels are clipped to [-2,2]; the same scoring mask and absolute-label weights apply to both losses. No teacher, distillation cache, initializer or parent state is admitted.

   The exact outer-fold manifest artifacts and hashes are not present in this source worktree, so cell membership is proposed but not fully frozen yet. Before admission, record each manifest SHA256, resolved train/evaluation component IDs and counts, raw input/data manifest and split-schema hashes, source SHA after commit, and the actual package/CUDA/driver/PyTorch environment. Do not substitute a row subset or infer component membership from fold names.

5. **Four paired fits.** Run exactly four scientific fits: F0/seed1201 × {WMSE, labels-NLL}, F2/seed1202 × {WMSE, labels-NLL}. These are two paired cells, not independent mechanism replications across a full fold/seed matrix. Do not count resource profiles as fits. A profile may precede admission only if its data, model shape, precision and loader settings match the screen and the measured projection leaves time for all four fits, independent grading, GPU cleanup and publication within the authorized wall-clock limit.

6. **Validation and significance.** Freeze epoch2 as the only endpoint; no within-fit outer-fold selection. Use the unchanged official `global_wp_clip2_v1` scorer and masks on each cell's complete excluded evaluation components. Pair candidate/control by component within each fold, report both cell deltas and the equal-weight mean across these two folds, alongside per-component deltas and a component-cluster interval. With only two exposed folds and one seed per fold, this is a low-power screen; an interval crossing zero is inconclusive, and no generalization or significance claim follows.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** NLL receives only `y[:, sl]` and `main_valid[:, sl]`; no teacher, warm initializer, cache or evaluation target enters optimization. Keep the source's causal raw inputs, sequence resets, fitting-only normalization and complete component exclusion. Report the exact source-qualified component list and sequence counts per fit and score. Previously exposed outer folds stay exposed. This result would concern a cold label-only objective at this exact schedule, not teacher-distilled NLL or every NLL recipe.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Continue only if labels-NLL is nonnegative in both cells, its paired component diagnostics show no concentrated regression, training is numerically stable, and the improvement is large enough to justify the variance head and its runtime cost. Otherwise retain WMSE as the control and treat NLL as unresolved or negative for this short cold recipe. Two cells cannot support a final promotion decision; they can justify a larger preregistered comparison or an efficient stop. Do not translate local deltas into public-score changes.

9. **How to run.** Use the exact command templates in [COMMANDS.md](COMMANDS.md) after replacing explicit placeholders with audited read-only paths/hashes. Set `WNN_PROJECT_ROOT` to the node's mounted project/data root and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to one assigned B300 per process. Capture device identity, driver, CUDA/PyTorch versions, CPU/RAM, package lock, effective loader workers, peak memory and full wall time. There is no DDP support in this path. First measure short canonical WMSE and NLL profiles; estimate each full three-epoch fit from timed optimizer steps including startup, data loading, evaluation/export and grader cost. If any endpoint cannot finish within the strict budget, do not admit a partial candidate/control pair as a completed comparison.

10. **Evidence to return.** Preserve each exact argv, source/dirty-patch hash, split and data-manifest hashes, environment lock, fit logs, all loss/gradient/update counters, epoch2 checkpoint SHA256, prediction and grade manifests, official grader output, per-cell/per-component metric table, elapsed phase times, peak RAM/VRAM and GPU utilization. Save evidence and weights separately. The coordinating operator owns GPU cleanup and repository publication under the separate authorization; this source packet contains no publication or execution receipt.

11. **Results and trace.** No cold-label fit, B300 profile, official score or public impact has been measured for this adaptation. The previous warm NLL result is only motivation and cannot be pooled with these cold cells. After source cross-review, append the local commit SHA and then the exact manifest/environment pins; after execution, append every fit, failure and exclusion, grader command/output, archive hashes, independent review, cleanup proof and publication link. No PR number, run ID or artifact hash is claimed here.


Operator verification: source `643c5cc55055ad98f79d0b1317462ed2e8fcf6af`; Ruff lint/format, AST and structure checks pass. Numerical pytest remains pending because the local verification environment has no PyTorch. SSH authentication was independently rejected by OpenSSH and Paramiko, so node assets, B300 profiles and execution are unverified. The 4-hour node wall includes profiling, fitting, evaluation, cleanup and publication; its clock has not started.

title: [Experiment] Run matched mask-aligned readout fits on B300
body:
# Run the four-fit mask-aligned readout experiment on B300

1. **Status and lineage.** Implements the existing #36 proposal on `experiment/mask-aligned-readout`, targeting `research-team`. This is a child of H-023/H-030/H-035 in the mask/propensity fine-tuning line, affecting the student/readout rather than the teacher or distillation link. Status: implemented, unvalidated on B300; zero new fits, profiles or evaluations. [README.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/README.md) contains executable receiver commands; [recipe.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/recipe.json) fixes the experiment. The original proposal is preserved in [PROPOSAL_20261022.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/PROPOSAL_20261022.md).

2. **Mechanism.** The competition objective uses scored rows, while the control trains on all valid prediction rows. Weighting fitting losses by real fitting-side `is_scored` may better align readout updates with that scored population. Expected observation: a positive matched treatment-minus-control weighted-Pearson delta. The frozen trunk and shared initialization isolate the readout-weighting intervention; parent quality, fold and seed remain confounded between cells. The public [MarkBrezina repository](https://github.com/MarkBrezina/WunderConnectome/tree/5d086fc90ea0c11a39391dde702e2a4f0a47a869) supplied an author-reported lead, not a verified competition result; no code or weights are copied.

3. **Compute advantage and budget.** Reuse two existing frozen GRU parents and train exactly four new heads. New parent fits: zero. Two bounded engineering profiles precede fitting and produce no scientific checkpoints. Full selected fitting components are used; there is no proxy subset, adaptive search or automatic budget expansion. Runtime savings and B300 throughput are unmeasured.

4. **Fixed comparison and implementation amendment.** Each cell starts both arms from identical pinned `@ep3` parent bytes. Freeze `inp,gru`, inherit preprocessing, use valid-side fitting data with fraction 1.0, clear propensity/class/episode weighting, and vary only `--mask-weight`. Both H256×2 parents retain WMSE and auxiliary coefficients 0.3/0.3, since-weight 32/floor 0.25. The canonical mask affects main **and auxiliary** loss weights: the estimand is explicitly scored-row weighting of the configured readout objective, not main WMSE alone. New fits use fresh AdamW LR 5e-4, weight decay 0.01, one-cycle scheduling, one epoch, batch 32, chunk 2000; fixed epoch 0 and no outer-fold evaluation during fitting. New computation is FP32, autocast/TF32 off. Exact historical FP16 parents are retained for this diagnostic; no end-to-end FP32-history claim. Before/after audits enforce frozen parameter and preprocessing invariance.

5. **Cells.** F0/seed1001 uses `oldz4_h230_parent_f0_s3_r3@ep3`; F2/seed1002 uses independent `h382_muonall256prop0_f2_s3_e4@ep3`. Each has `all_valid` and `is_scored_weighted`, giving four fits total. Checkpoint, provenance and split SHA-256 pins live in the recipe. Missing artifacts stop execution; no silent alternate checkpoint or cross-fold substitution.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Canonical `global_wp_clip2_v1`, targets/predictions clipped to [-2,2], complete held-out coverage and scoring on `need_prediction & is_scored`. Primary: treatment-minus-control delta per fold and equal-cell mean, with per-target scores. Use the canonical paired whole-component bootstrap, 10,000 replicates per fold and independent streams from seed 221022; average matched fold draws to obtain the equal-cell interval. It measures conditional component-sampling sensitivity, not fit/seed/parent uncertainty. Both folds have previous exposure; this is a two-cell screen, not a significance claim. Secondary: unchanged parent, fixed 0.75-parent/0.25-child blends, their deltas against the parent and treatment-blend minus control-blend. No weight search.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** `train.parquet` lacks `is_scored`; this head-fit experiment uses the real mask only on valid-side fitting components. It never constructs a train-side pseudo-mask or feeds masks into the model. Canonical campaign splits bind source-qualified fitting/evaluation membership; held-out components are excluded from fit weights, preprocessing and checkpoint selection. Parent preprocessing and frozen tensors must remain unchanged; prediction export is feature-only. Legacy parents are checked against exact pinned artifacts and recorded provenance, without pretending they contain newer metadata. Unknown historical ancestry is not upgraded to a new clean-history certificate.

8. **Decision.** Mean paired primary delta ≥ +0.0003 and both cells nonnegative supports a separately budgeted confirmation. Mixed signs are uncertain; an interval crossing zero alone is not a kill rule. Both cells below the useful threshold narrow or stop this exact recipe. A missing asset, source/membership mismatch or failed finite-update/memory check stops the current run rather than changing the experiment. Wider temporal/regime generalization and submission value remain unknown.

9. **Execution.** [receiver.py](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/receiver.py) orchestrates the existing `scripts/train_rnn.py` and `scripts/predict_run.py`; it does not duplicate the trainer. Provide [receiver-assets.example.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/receiver-assets.example.json), install the locked Linux CUDA environment, and invoke `preflight → profile → fit → predict → score` as documented in [README.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/README.md). Profiles prove actual trainer-process B300 UUID, driver, strict FP32, finite updates and ≥10% memory headroom. New child provenance captures that actual-process runtime. Source identity includes all Python under `src`; evaluator identity additionally binds packet code and prediction entrypoint. Snapshot fields recording no execution in this delivery are not runtime permission gates: a future explicit receiver command is the operator's execution decision.

10. **Returned evidence.** Persist profile receipts; exact parent, split and source hashes; head-only trainables; frozen-state and preprocessing identities; child provenance/checkpoints; full-coverage predictions and their hashes; and `grade.json` with paired intervals, all secondary endpoints, target-cache, recipe, audit and evaluator-source bindings. Keep failures and do not silently overwrite prior artifacts. Scientific checkpoints and heavy weights remain separate from code/evidence. Actual runtime, memory and scores are not populated with estimates.

11. **Validation performed and limitations.** Static source, formatting and structural checks are recorded in [VALIDATION.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/716dbde5451726c0d01790638fded6d23a99de05/research/experiment_drafts/mask-aligned-readout/VALIDATION.json). Receiver tests are provided for later execution. Local tests, training, model inference and B300 jobs were not run. This PR contains runnable implementation and explicit missing-asset checks; it does not claim a successful GPU run or a submission improvement.

title: [Experiment] Run matched numerical-input Transformers on B300
body:
# Run the fixed numerical-input Transformer comparison on B300

This implements the six-fit experiment from #35. All three arms retain raw112,
causal event99 and missing112 inputs; uniform16 and quantile16 add equal-sized
piecewise-linear branches. The primary question is whether fitting-distribution
knot placement helps more than evenly spaced knots. It targets the teacher's
input representation, building on #8/#31; no teacher/student link is tested here.

## Expected mechanism and decision

A shared linear map may represent nonlinear threshold effects inefficiently.
If knot placement is the useful mechanism, quantile16 should beat uniform16 on
both fixed cells without simply benefiting from extra parameters. Raw contrasts
are secondary and capacity-confounded. Report F0/1001 and F2/1002, both targets,
all arms, and paired whole-component uncertainty. Mean +0.0003 with consistent
cells supports a larger independent confirmation; conflicting cells or an
interval crossing zero are inconclusive. A clear practically negative effect
rejects this bounded recipe, not every numerical representation. All folds have
been exposed; this screen cannot establish generalization or statistical significance.

## Included implementation

- Reuses the pinned #32 trainer, merged into this branch for a self-contained checkout.
- Shared fitting-only normalization and immutable, source-bound knot artifact;
  bounded seeded reservoir quantiles with full-fit endpoints (explicit prospective
  amendment before any outcomes, detailed in README).
- Matched common initialization, zero-initialized basis, FP32 RoPE Transformer,
  WSD schedule, one-GPU/global-batch32 enforcement and fixed epoch11 endpoint.
- Six consumable configs and single-cell prepare/profile/fit/evaluate commands,
  checkpoint/resume support, causal cached inference and canonical pooled grading.
- Panel grader verifies shared data/preprocessing/source/runtime/initialization,
  reports all contrasts, and computes equal-cell CIs from independent fold draws.
- Receiver tests for missing inputs, fitting-only artifact membership, tied bins,
  prefix causality, full/chunk/row parity, serialization and common initialization.

The full fitting set is used after warmup; the train parquet has no scored mask.
Evaluation alone uses the true scored mask. Calibration never uses labels or
held-out features. More GPU spend can scale teacher capacity/confirmation later;
this screen fixes six complete fits and does not measure a pay-to-win scaling law.
CPU student inference, 20-MB packaging and quantization remain separate.

## Validation and handoff

Static formatting/lint, AST structure checks and source review only. **No local
tests, training, inference or GPU jobs were run.** Device fit, performance and
quality are unmeasured. The receiver must bind the actual source/split assets,
run the written acceptance checks and approve successful real-shape B300 profiles
before fitting. A failed profile requires an explicit recipe amendment, not a
silent batch/precision change.

See [receiver commands](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/eed60073e8b1a656fe91dd397498b2b8843163ad/research/experiment_drafts/typed-bin-feature-encoding/README.md), [frozen recipe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/eed60073e8b1a656fe91dd397498b2b8843163ad/research/experiment_drafts/typed-bin-feature-encoding/recipe.json),
[static validation](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/eed60073e8b1a656fe91dd397498b2b8843163ad/research/experiment_drafts/typed-bin-feature-encoding/VALIDATION.json), and [original proposal](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/eed60073e8b1a656fe91dd397498b2b8843163ad/research/experiment_drafts/typed-bin-feature-encoding/PROPOSAL_20261022.md).

Evidence, failed attempts, hypothesis progression and exact artifacts are indexed in `research/campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/FRONTIER.md` and unified notes. # [Experiment] large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2: teacher quality, scaling and event dynamics

Latest user amendment: **teacher quality first; distillation optional**. The
[scaling programme](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/unified/ideas/TEACHER_QUALITY_SCALING_20261019_R1.md) proposes a six-fit 0.2/0.68/1.65B ladder, equal-data/equal-compute curves, repeated-data diagnostics and ranked tuning. This is the current strategic priority. Existing four-fit JSON panels below remain prior unlaunched proposals; receiver must explicitly replace the selected recipe and freeze its budget before launch. No extra panel is implicitly admitted.

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Proposed teacher-scale recipe; root owns design,
   receiving B300 implementer owns source binding and execution. H-LARGE-DYNAMICS-TEACHER-20261019-R2;
   E-LARGE-DYNAMICS-TEACHER-SCALE-20261019-R2. Builds on the earlier AR/grouped-input
   proposals; not a claim that their trainers or fits completed. This draft
   supplies a recipe and analytical calculator, not a new executable DDP trainer.
2. **Why it should work.** Latest user source [TradeFM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23784) motivates an additional, separately budgeted [event-objective contrast](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/TRADEFM_ADAPTATION.md): predict observable-change hazards and marks while retaining supervised per-row targets. This is the preferred first dynamics screen; it does not import proprietary data, real-unit feature assumptions or a market simulator.

 A larger causal teacher may represent conditional
   cross-feature dynamics that a compact recurrent teacher misses. Compare0.68B
   and 1.65B capacity recipes at the same context/data/row budget. Alternatives:
   repeated-data overfitting, bad optimization or capacity that cannot transfer.
   Grouped numeric encoding, auxiliary future-observation targets and full-history
   attention are separately budgeted descendants rather than a confounded grid.
3. **Compute advantage.** Eight B300s support replicated large teachers and
   longer contextual training. Profile8-way versus two 4-way jobs at the same
   global batch. DDP does not pool memory. First flagship 1.65B,0.68B reference,
  3.17B eligible extension. No local score, scaling law or B300 speed is promised.
4. **Frozen comparison.** The proposed two arms use 24×1536/FF4096 and 32×2048/FF5632
   dense causal trunks,64-dimensional heads, raw 112+canonical event 99 inputs,
   strict FP32 with autocast/TF32 off. Start4096-row windows/2048 new-row cores,
   nominal 65,536 new rows/update,12-epoch cooled endpoint. FP32 Muon match_rms_adamw
   hidden-matrix groups; AdamW input/readout/norm groups; peak base LR1e-4 versus
  7.5e-5, momentum 0.95,5 NS iterations, gradient clip 1.0, declared decay groups.
   The scale-specific LR makes this a capacity-RECIPE comparison. WSD uses the
   same 1500-update initial warmup, stable prefix, final 20% cosine cooldown to 0.1×.
   Exact component membership, normalized objective, shapes and source are still
   unbound; launch_ready=false. AR/auxiliary/long-memory are off in this first pair.
5. **Bounded fitting panel.** Each panel has four total new teacher fits. The new transition_recipe.json compares auxiliary likelihood off/on at the same0.68B scale in two cells. The original capacity recipe below is a SEPARATE four-fit contrast; running both costs eight teacher fits before students. Neither panel is automatically funded. Capacity panel: two arms each at
   F0/seed 1001 and F2/seed 1002, subject to ownership and frozen split binding.
   No mandatory CP30. No cached controls or student fits are counted here.
   Student transfer needs its own 4–6-fit inventory with teacher caches named.
   Expanded panels require a dated allocation; engineering profiles are separate
   charged work and not scientific replications.
6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Unchanged global_wp_clip2_v1 on the fixed
   official mask and source-qualified held-out components. Report both paired
   deltas and their descriptive mean, conditional component sensitivity and
   by-target/activity/sequence-age diagnostics. Two cells do not identify seed
   versus fold variability or establish significance. All folds remain exposed;
   no public-score forecast. Retain all failures and selection history.
7. **Leakage and coverage.** Teachers, initializers, normalizers and auxiliary
   transforms exclude evaluated components. No lagged true labels, full-sequence
   normalization or future-containing patch summaries. Later slow tokens become
   visible only after their block completes. Require numerical causality/reset,
   weighted-DDP and producer-consumer checks before fitting. A production all-data
   teacher is separate from held-out evidence.
8. **Decision-changing result.** A useful teacher gain with compatible regimes
   justifies matched GRU distillation; smaller or mixed effects may justify
   mechanisms, optimizer/context repairs or teacher-mixture tests. Negative results
   narrow the tested capacity recipe. A zero-crossing interval alone does not
   close scale. Final priority is a stronger GRU or complete served blend, not
   teacher parameter count. Student transfer remains untested.
9. **How to run.** Implemented commands are only the stdlib capacity calculator
   and plan expander listed in README. No torchrun command is advertised as
   runnable. The receiving implementer must add canonical-component model/DDP
   integration, source-bound folds/data, an audited FP32 Muon path, backend/dtype
   checks and actual-shape profiles; then record exact torchrun arguments and
  8-card reservation. Current source Muon casts NS work to BF16 and needs adaptation.
10. **Evidence to return.** Immutable source/config/env/split/ancestry, exact
    commands and actual devices; attempted/successful steps, loss components,
    LR, preclip norms/clipping, finite/update checks, processed/new-row throughput,
    memory, checkpoint/resume identities and official predictions/grades.
    Separate checksummed evidence/weights archives in private storage, no raw
    dataset upload. Include teacher export and student fitting costs in total ETA.
11. **Results and trace.** No new fit or empirical improvement. The unified
    [design](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/unified/ideas/LARGE_DYNAMICS_TRANSFORMER_B300_20261019_R2.md),
    [sources](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/unified/sources/TRANSFORMER_B300_SCALE_SOURCES_20261019_R2.md)
    and [independent review](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/unified/reviews/LARGE_TEACHER_DESIGN_REVIEW_20261019_R2.md)
    preserve the reasoning and remaining checks. Older stopped B300 GRU evidence
    is not Transformer evidence. Publication/source/base links must name actual
    commits after this draft is created. No model launch or competition upload.

User-paper addendum: [TradeFM adaptation](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/TRADEFM_ADAPTATION.md), [transition recipe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/transition_recipe.json), and [explicit four-fit plan](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/TRANSITION_PLAN.json). Paper generation quality is not evidence for our official WP or student quality. Strict-FP32 Muon remains a proposed adaptation, not the source paper recipe.

title: [Experiment] Streaming Transformer students versus GRU with matched KD
body:
# [Experiment] Compact streaming Transformer students with matched label/KD controls

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** This is an amended prospective PR30 panel with four new student fits, not the original 180-fit CP30 design. The shared training runtime is implemented in draft [PR #32](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32), but no profile, fit, score, or B300 acceptance was performed for this panel. Runtime source is pinned to `d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6`; the docs/base-sync HEAD is `d7559e94`. The panel targets `research-team`; no training authorization is implied. See [runtime amendment](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/streaming-student-distillation/RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md), [machine-readable amendment](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/streaming-student-distillation/runtime_amendment.json), frozen [historical recipe](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/streaming-student-distillation/recipe.json), and byte-preserved [original PR body](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/streaming-student-distillation/PR_CP30_FROZEN.md).

2. **Question.** Does output distillation improve a compact raw-112 Transformer over its same-cell label-only control, and how does its KD endpoint compare with the exact PR28 GRU-KD endpoint? The cross-architecture comparison is descriptive: model shapes, parameters and FLOPs are not matched. Existing rationale is in [Section 25 of the canonical note](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/unified/ideas/CAUSAL_AR_TRANSFORMER_GRU_DISTILLATION_B300_20261017_R1.md#25-distill-to-the-architecture-we-can-actually-serve).

3. **Why this is useful.** A bounded streaming Transformer may transfer behavior that differs from the recurrent baseline, while its actual inference cost remains unknown. Same-architecture label-only controls isolate the incremental KD contrast. The two-cell panel is a focused executable amendment, not a replacement for the historical broader architecture/window portfolio and not evidence of CPU deployment value.

4. **Frozen configs and objective.** New fits are F0/seed1001 and F2/seed1002, each with `student_t128_labels` and `student_t128_kd`. The model consumes 112 raw features and uses width128, two layers, four heads, FFN multiplier4, dropout0, and sliding KV context128 per layer. Each run uses three epochs, batch1, four accumulated 256-row chunks, AdamW LR`3e-4`, weight decay`.01`, clip`1.0`, warmup fraction`.05`, and the first32 fitting sequences for normalization. The label arm uses `label WMSE + 0 × KD WMSE`; KD uses `label WMSE + 1.0 × KD WMSE`. Both configs retain a learned 64-dimensional hint projection with hint weight0, as required by the shared model schema. All arithmetic is strict FP32; autocast, GradScaler, TF32, and quantization are disabled. Exact runtime configs are under `research/experiment_drafts/b300-transformer-distillation-runtime/configs/` at the pinned runtime source.

5. **Four new fits and reuse.** PR30 adds four student fits. It reuses two exact T768×24 teacher models/caches and four GRU256 label/KD endpoints from PR28: F0/student seed1001/teacher seed101001 and F2/student seed1002/teacher seed101002. Reuse is valid only when source, split/component membership, config, seed, cache manifest, and endpoint hashes match. A mismatch requires a separately reviewed source/cache binding; do not reuse by filename.

6. **Primary comparison and interpretation.** The primary contrasts are KD minus label-only within F0/seed1001 and F2/seed1002. Report both folds and both targets, pooled official `global_wp_clip2_v1`, uncertainty, memory/time, and the exact matched controls. A `+0.001 WP` gain is a useful signal for a bounded follow-up, not an automatic promotion rule. A smaller or mixed result, or an interval crossing zero, is not an automatic rejection. The comparison to PR28 GRU-KD is secondary and is not parameter- or FLOP-matched. Do not infer replication or generalization from two exposed cells.

7. **Causal and data controls.** Bind canonical source-qualified F0/F2 splits, component manifests, fitting membership, normalizer, teacher checkpoint/cache provenance, and all input hashes before admission. Forward complete ordered sequences from row zero and reset state per sequence. Warm-up rows0–98 remain in the forward pass but are excluded from the fit/score mask. Preserve source/target row alignment and teacher mapping; no teacher output is an inference-time feature. Apply only the fixed terminal epoch, with no outer-validation checkpoint selection.

8. **Risks and falsifiers.** The architecture comparison has unequal shapes and possibly unequal compute; it cannot establish architecture superiority at equal parameters/FLOPs. Output KD may fail to improve its matched labels-only student. Sliding-cache correctness, B300 performance, resource headroom and eventual CPU serving remain unmeasured until receiving-host checks. A positive KD result alone does not establish a deployable model or justify quantization.

9. **How to run after admission.** First complete the [PR32 remote acceptance checklist](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6/research/experiment_drafts/b300-transformer-distillation-runtime/REMOTE_ACCEPTANCE.md). On the allocated host, create a detached checkout at the pinned implementation and verify `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6`; then run `uv sync --frozen`, bind approved data/split/output roots, and establish a fresh real-shape eight-update profile for every config. Record the profile review and approved receipt before any scientific fit. Use the four exact config paths and separate output/profile directories shown in the [amendment commands](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/experiment_drafts/streaming-student-distillation/RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md#admission-commands-and-outputs). KD fits require the matching PR28 teacher cache; label-only fits reject a teacher cache. Preserve exact configuration and identity fields on resume.

10. **Evidence to return.** For each profile and fit, retain source/config/data/split/cache hashes; runtime, device and precision metadata; attempted/successful updates; losses, LR, gradient and finite-status diagnostics; throughput, peak allocated/reserved memory, terminal status; model/checkpoint hashes; full-sequence predictions and official score. Retain failed attempts. Export, scoring and CPU release checks follow the pinned runtime contracts. Keep weights and private data out of Git and attach separate hash-bound evidence/weight archives on the receiving host.

11. **Results and trace.** No results exist: the four fits, profiles, exports and scores are absent, and B300 acceptance is pending. This packet makes no CPU-serving, one-core/16-GB/60-minute, ZIP-readiness or public-score claim. The original CP30 `recipe.json` remains unchanged and is historical only. See [PR32 runtime](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32), [canonical rationale](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/unified/ideas/CAUSAL_AR_TRANSFORMER_GRU_DISTILLATION_B300_20261017_R1.md), and [CPU inference contract](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/streaming-student-distillation/research/unified/inference/TRANSFORMER_DISTILLATION_CPU_PATH.md). Append actual receipts and results without replacing historical records.

title: [Experiment] Causal teacher hints beyond output distillation
body:
# [Experiment] Causal teacher hints beyond two-output distillation

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** This updates PR #29 for H-TEACHER-REPRESENTATION-HINTS-20261019 / E-TEACHER-REPRESENTATION-HINTS-20261019. The runtime dependency is implemented in [PR #32](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32) at source commit [d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/commit/d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6); this four-fit PR29 panel remains unprofiled and unrun, with launch readiness false. The original CP30 text is frozen in [PR_CP30_FROZEN.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-representation-hints/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-representation-hints/PR_CP30_FROZEN.md), and the historical [recipe.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-representation-hints/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-representation-hints/recipe.json) is unchanged. Root maintains this design; the receiving operator claims cells and binds data/artifacts. No result is claimed.

2. **Why it should work.** Two-output KD can omit useful temporal structure in a strong teacher's hidden state. Add a 64-dimensional fit-time representation target while keeping output KD fixed. Compare aligned teacher/student rows against output-only KD and against a component-permuted hint target. H−O tests whether hints add value; H−P tests whether alignment matters beyond adding the same auxiliary loss. Generic regularization or donor-distribution effects remain plausible alternatives.

3. **Compute advantage.** The amendment spends four new GRU256 fits across two cells and reuses the two exact same-fold PR28 teacher/cache pairs and output-KD controls. No teacher fit is added. The value sought is stronger student learning per added student fit; cache I/O is a known cost (64 hint values per row versus two output values). This screen has not measured throughput, memory, score gain or serving feasibility.

4. **Frozen comparison.** New arms H and P use raw112 inputs, canonical GRU256×2, fitting-only normalization over the first 32 fitting sequences, full 20,000-row sequence traversal, 256-row TBPTT chunks, reset between sequences, three fixed epochs, batch size one per rank and four-chunk accumulation. Strict FP32 is used for parameters, states, activations, gradients and AdamW; autocast, GradScaler, TF32 and quantization are off. AdamW uses LR 3e-4, weight decay 0.01, 5% warmup and gradient clipping at 1.0. The shared same-fold T768×24 teacher/cache uses 512-row sliding KV per layer and a frozen seed-1729 projection of its per-row-normalized final hidden state. The student projection is learned and omitted at inference. The additive objective is WMSE(clipped labels) + 1.0*WMSE(clipped teacher outputs) + 0.1*MSE(hints); label and KD terms use abs(clipped label) weights. The mask is is_scored AND row_index >= 99; all rows still update causal state. The endpoint is the configured final epoch. This is not the historical alpha=0.9 mixture.

5. **Bounded four-fit panel.** This is an explicitly bounded screen, not CP30: cells F0/student seed 1001/teacher seed 101001 and F2/student seed 1002/teacher seed 101002. Each cell reuses one output-KD control and one same-fold teacher/cache, then adds one H and one P fit. That is four new fits total, two reused controls and two reused teacher/cache pairs. The historical 30-cell-per-arm design remains preserved but is not being run by this amendment. Two cells do not support confirmatory across-seed or unseen-fold claims.

6. **Validation and significance.** Grade each endpoint with the pinned runtime's canonical global_wp_clip2_v1 pooled scorer on the identical held-out scored rows, excluding warmup rows 0–98. Report H−O and H−P for each fold, each target, and pooled official score; retain the source-qualified component breakdown. With one seed per fold, component resampling over fixed predictions is sensitivity analysis only. Do not present it as seed uncertainty or a calibrated confidence interval. Both folds are exposed.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Reuse only PR28 teachers/caches whose complete ancestry has the same fold hash and exact source-qualified fitting membership, excluding evaluation components. Teacher targets on fitting components are in-sample by design. The P arm rotates fitting-component donors while keeping row position and aligned output-KD targets. Teacher outputs and hints are training-only; no teacher signal enters student inference. Preserve complete causal rows, warmup, reset and source-qualified membership.

8. **Decision-changing result.** H should improve over O to support added hint value, and H−P helps distinguish aligned representation learning from an unaligned auxiliary loss. A descriptive +0.001 WP signal is useful for deciding whether to follow up, not a pass/fail boundary. Smaller or mixed effects and an interval crossing zero do not automatically reject the mechanism; they can motivate a targeted continuation. Inspect both targets, both folds, actual compute and the separate CPU-serving gate. A result that beats P but not O does not establish benefit beyond output KD.

9. **How to run.** On the receiving host, fetch the runtime PR and pin the executable checkout before using its packet configs. Set thread and deterministic CUDA environment variables from the complete setup block in [RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-representation-hints/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-representation-hints/RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md):

   ~~~bash
   git fetch origin refs/pull/32/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr-32-runtime
   git switch --detach d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6
   test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6
   uv sync --frozen
   export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src"
   test -n "$WNN_DATA_ROOT"
   test -n "$WNN_SPLIT_F0"
   test -n "$WNN_SPLIT_F2"
   test -n "$WNN_RUN_ROOT"
   test -n "$WNN_T768_F0_CACHE"
   test -n "$WNN_T768_F2_CACHE"
   ~~~

   First complete the pinned runtime's remote acceptance and actual-shape review. Profile each of the four configs in the [runtime packet](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6/research/experiment_drafts/b300-transformer-distillation-runtime/README.md), using one GPU, eight updates, a fresh output directory and the matching teacher cache. Review and approve each matching receipt. The profile-to-fit command pair and all four config pins are in the [runtime amendment](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-representation-hints/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-representation-hints/RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md). Run the full fit with the same config/data/split/cache arguments, a fresh fit directory and the approved profile receipt. Export each completed endpoint with scripts/predict_sequence.py --membership evaluation and grade with scripts/score_sequence.py. No data paths or existing artifact hashes are fabricated.

10. **Evidence to return.** Bind each cell to exact runtime/config/data/split/teacher/checkpoint/cache hashes and environment. Preserve profile receipts, fit progress, successful updates, losses, LR, preclip gradient norm, nonfinite counts, memory/time, full predictions, per-target/fold official grades, component breakdowns and terminal status. Retain failures. Bundle evidence and weights separately with SHA256 and approved private storage paths. The separate [CPU inference contract](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/research-team/research/unified/inference/TRANSFORMER_DISTILLATION_CPU_PATH.md) still governs release feasibility.

11. **Results and trace.** No PR29 profile, fit, prediction export, grade, GPU acceptance or public-score forecast has been produced. The [canonical rationale](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/research-team/research/unified/ideas/CAUSAL_AR_TRANSFORMER_GRU_DISTILLATION_B300_20261017_R1.md), [runtime PR #32](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32), and [runtime amendment](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-representation-hints/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-representation-hints/RUNTIME_AMENDMENT.md) define the design and implementation lineage. Append actual source/merge SHAs and cell receipts when available; preserve this historical CP30 record unchanged.

title: [Experiment] Teacher scale × GRU capacity transfer frontier
body:
# [Experiment] Teacher scale × GRU transfer: explicit raw112 runtime amendment

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** This is a prospective amendment to the published design [PR #28](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/28), associated with `H-TEACHER-TRANSFER-FRONTIER-20261019` and `E-TEACHER-TRANSFER-FRONTIER-20261019`. The original CP30 body is preserved byte-for-byte in [PR_CP30_FROZEN.md](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-transfer-frontier/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-transfer-frontier/PR_CP30_FROZEN.md); [recipe.json](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/teacher-transfer-frontier/research/experiment_drafts/teacher-transfer-frontier/recipe.json) also remains unchanged and describes that historical CP30 design. This prospective panel depends on the implemented but unexecuted shared runtime in [PR #32](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/32), pinned to source commit [`d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6`](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/commit/d2e6263af3a0dcb2d35badec8c3fa15da0d91dc6). Runtime code is not copied into this packet. The scientific panel is unrun: no receiving-host checks, profiles, fits, grades or measured B300 result are claimed. Root owns the design; the receiving operator must bind the data/splits, claim cells and own execution.

2. **Why it should work.** A stronger causal teacher may improve a compact student, but teacher quality alone does not establish transfer. Compare a matched GRU trained on labels with the same GRU trained using the frozen teacher’s outputs. This bounded screen tests transfer for the T768×24 teacher and GRU256 student in two paired cells; it does not test the wider historical scale frontier.

3. **Compute advantage.** The amended first panel costs six new fits: two T768×24 teachers, two GRU256 label controls and two GRU256 KD students. Teacher fits create reusable same-fold caches; student fits test their downstream value. The teacher is not counted as an independent replication of its students. This allocation is not an eight-GPU-hour reservation or a throughput claim. Further teacher/student scale work remains a separately admitted follow-up.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Use two cells: F0/student seed 1001/teacher seed 101001 and F2/student seed 1002/teacher seed 101002. Each cell fits one teacher, one GRU256 label control and one GRU256 KD student. The teacher is a raw112 causal Transformer, width 768, 24 layers, 12 heads, FF multiplier 4, 512-row per-layer sliding KV context, zero dropout and activation checkpointing. GRU students use the canonical GRU adapter, hidden 256×2, raw112 input and recurrent state that resets at each sequence boundary. All fits use strict FP32 parameters, activations, states, gradients and optimizer; autocast, GradScaler, TF32 and quantization are off. They train three fixed epochs, full 20,000-row sequences in 256-row chunks, TBPTT state detach at chunk boundaries and AdamW with cosine schedule, gradient clip 1.0, weight decay 0.01 and 5% warmup. Teacher LR is 1e-4; student LR is 3e-4. Normalization is fitted on the first 32 fitting sequences only; score/loss mask is `is_scored & row>=99`. The additive objective is `WMSE(clipped labels) + kd_weight*WMSE(clipped teacher outputs) + hint_weight*MSE(hints)`; label and KD terms use absolute clipped-label weights. Teacher has KD/hint weights zero; label student has KD/hint weights zero; KD student has KD weight 1.0 and hint weight zero. No alpha=0.9 mixture or anchored4096 procedure carries forward.

5. **Bounded fitting panel.** The six new fits are:

   | Cell | Teacher | Label control | KD student |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | F0 / s1001 | `teacher_t768_l24_f0_s1001.json` | `gru256_labels_f0_s1001.json` | `gru256_kd_f0_s1001.json` |
   | F2 / s1002 | `teacher_t768_l24_f2_s1002.json` | `gru256_labels_f2_s1002.json` | `gru256_kd_f2_s1002.json` |

   Total: 2 teacher fits + 4 student fits = 6 new fits; no control or cache reuse is claimed for this first panel. These two cells confound fold and fitting seed and are a descriptive screen, not CP30. Hints and streaming are separate four-fit panels that may reuse only these exact hash-bound teacher caches/endpoints after this panel is completed and independently checked. No follow-up launches automatically.

6. **Validation and uncertainty.** Score with the canonical pooled `global_wp_clip2_v1` on exact held-out component membership; report both targets and each cell. Primary transfer contrast is GRU256 KD minus GRU256 labels within each cell; teacher score is reported separately and cannot substitute for student transfer. Two cells do not estimate training variance, support significance, or establish generalization. # [Experiment] E-B300-R01: cold GRU width versus depth at fixed training budget

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** H-B300-R01 / E-B300-R01, labels-only student capacity branch; owned by SemyonEpanov's authorized tabdata campaign. This registers an already frozen and executing experiment, not a new prospective preregistration. Sixty strict-FP32 fits are planned. This is distinct from #2: near parameter counts and fixed updates, not matched measured FLOPs. Scientific source a266b036b02e8e012c6eb31072291dad618a169d; source-tree SHA256 `f4ef9ca8450a3e76d6b6f8295259e70aec5024d3a4f3296558bb0323add74130`. No teacher or pretrained initializer.

2. **Why it should work.** A deeper recurrent composition may represent temporal interactions more efficiently than width alone. Predicted observation: deep-minus-wide gains across matched seeds and folds, rather than only one favorable fold. Additional optimization difficulty or unmatched arithmetic cost are competing explanations. This experiment estimates a fixed-recipe capacity contrast; it cannot establish a general depth scaling law.

3. **Compute advantage.** Eight B300s provide 30 independent paired fitting cells per arm. Four measured concurrent actors per GPU share capacity with the separate PR15 experiment. Additional compute buys replication, not an assumed leaderboard gain. Serving cost and downstream distillation require separate evidence.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Wide GRU H512x1 (2,210,306 parameters) versus deep H384x2 (2,151,554); wide is 2.73% larger. Input: 112 raw plus 99 canonical event features. Fit-only two-batch normalization, labels-only loss, batch8, context/chunk2000, six complete epochs, fixed epoch5 checkpoint. AdamW lr1e-4, beta2=.999, weight decay=.01, OneCycle warmup=.05, clipping1, dropout0. Strict FP32, autocast and TF32 disabled. Same fold/seed controls, no teacher, initialization warm start or automatic scientific retries. The frozen execution manifest is `95f82d442eefe425dde6574222b037ba1deba2d3ae36534aeec41e31e450874f`.

5. **Thirty paired runs.** Per arm: F0/F1 seeds1003..1010, F2/F3 seeds1003..1009, an 8/8/7/7 matrix. Seeds1001/1002 remain externally owned and excluded. Panel SHA256 `471f465cc1d13fc6e5153a4c998390bb14e06823fed4c6721f929ce95fee47fb`; all sixty cells retain distinct fit claims. Resource profiles are excluded from replication counts.

6. **Validation and significance.** Unchanged `global_wp_clip2_v1`, official target mask, component-qualified evaluation. Primary statistic: equal-fold mean of matched deep-minus-wide WP. Frozen 10,000 shared-fitting-seed bootstrap replicates, RNG271828; component uncertainty is evaluated separately. These are exposed development folds; fitting-seed intervals do not quantify selection or public-transfer uncertainty. Partial tables are descriptive and are not significance tests.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Frozen fold membership, fitting-only normalization and past-only recurrent inputs apply. No labels enter feature assembly. Source-qualified sequence/component identities must match fit/export/grade manifests; cross-fold evaluation is robustness evidence, not a pristine holdout. This capacity comparison does not establish representativeness for unobserved market regimes.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Frozen decision SHA256 `32a9f0aaee4a0a839468c618853ec441d65e5bce91860a5b202454e931b235d7`. A useful absolute WP difference of .001 guides follow-up spending; it is not a universal significance threshold. Assess quality alongside measured runtime and serving cost. title: [Experiment] Four-arm GRU, Transformer and Mamba-2 handoff
body:
# [Experiment] GRU / causal Transformer / Mamba-2: published source and CP30 handoff

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Source-preservation and integration proposal, E-ARCHITECTURE-CP30-HANDOFF-20261018; H-CAUSAL-TRANSFORMER-20261017, H-CONTEXT-TRANSFORMER-20261017 and H-SELECTIVE-SSM-20261017. The prepared implementation exists at `bd78ac1048fe9d6534e76cde8c6f8ec0d6aa6acb` on `codex/transformer-mamba-gpu-wave`. It uses an older trainer and an unrun single-F0/seed3/one-epoch screen. This PR adds a current-base handoff, not an automatic merge of that trainer or a claim of executed experiments. Receiving run owner and current executable source are unbound; launch_ready=false and training_authorized=false.

2. **Why it should work.** At the same label objective, attention may retain useful selected history beyond the GRU state; extending its window tests whether additional past context matters. Mamba-2 tests selective state-space recurrence. These are candidate mechanisms, not evidence of a win. Architecture dimensions, parameter counts, optimization behavior and compute differ; a quality difference does not uniquely identify memory as the cause. C−B isolates the declared window change; B−A and D−A compare complete model families under a common declared recipe.

3. **Compute advantage.** More GPUs buy independent paired cells and, separately, larger teachers or longer training. This comparison spends on full-data repetitions before selecting a family. No scaling law, B300 throughput or public-score forecast is asserted. Report both equal-exposure endpoints and actual GPU time/memory; a compute-matched comparison would require its own frozen budget and endpoints. A teacher improvement requires a later matched compact-GRU KD test, not a promised student gain.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Proposed A=GRU256×2; B=causal Transformer256×4/8heads/FFN4/window256; C=same/window2048; D=Mamba-2 width256/layers4/state64/head64/expand2/conv4/chunk256. Same complete source-qualified fitting membership, 211 inputs, labels-only objective, cold seeded initialization policy, row order, normalization membership, loss weights, optimizer/update schedule and fixed final checkpoint. Match paired initialization only where shapes permit; different model shapes cannot have identical tensors. Freeze six full epochs, fixed epoch5, no best-validation selection. Exact common optimizer/LR/clip/batch/update budget and stable attention/SSM implementations remain binding gates; do not claim the old one-epoch runner already implements this plan. Strict FP32 weights/states/activations/gradients/optimizer; autocast/GradScaler/TF32 off. The legacy wave only requested FP32; its TF32-off path is unverified. Current adapters must enforce and record actual precision. Reset all model/feature/cache state per sequence and serialize complete architecture state for exact resume, or restart under a new attempt ID.

5. **Thirty paired runs.** F0/F1 seeds1001–1008 and F2/F3 seeds1001–1007, 30 cells for each of A/B/C/D, **120 fits total**. Three preregistered contrasts B−A, C−B and D−A. Original F0/seed3 screen and engineering profiles do not count. All folds are exposed. Bind data/split hashes, fit-only normalization and ancestry per cell; no production train+valid checkpoint may be relabeled as a clean held-out parent.

6. **Validation and significance.** Unchanged global_wp_clip2_v1 and official masks. For each contrast compute D=mean_f(mean_s(per-fit paired WP delta)), with four equal fold weights. Reuse the workflow's 10000 shared-seed bootstrap draws and separate paired component resampling, RNG20261018; eight seed identities are not 30 IID holdouts. Report marginal95% and Bonferroni98.3333% intervals for the three-contrast family, all fold means, costs, failures and exclusions. These are approximate conditional intervals, not a guarantee of power, new-regime coverage or calibrated significance. A seed ensemble or blend is a different endpoint and cannot replace the declared contrast.

7. **Leakage and coverage.** Past/current supplied features only; no future label/target inputs, bidirectional attention or cross-sequence state. Sliding-window cache, Mamba recurrent state and input transforms must pass suffix/prefix/reset/chunk invariance checks on the receiving GPU. Fold-clean normalizers and complete connected-component exclusion remain mandatory. No ranking by public leaderboard feedback. Compare any later promising endpoint against a source-qualified strong baseline; the production TL3 ensemble is not a clean F0 control.

8. **Decision-changing result.** Proposed useful threshold D≥+0.0005 WP per primary contrast, with compatible family-adjusted seed/component intervals and fold robustness; this is an allocation criterion, not a predicted effect. Report cost before deciding whether the gain merits a downstream KD comparison. No speed/CPU claim follows. Inconclusive intervals may justify bounded precision follow-up; a negative result narrows the declared model/context/optimizer budget. No dependency or profile failure is a scientific rejection.

9. **How to run.** From a complete current checkout, `python scripts/experiment_draft_plan.py research/experiment_drafts/architecture-cp30-handoff/recipe.json` prints metadata only; it was not run. There is deliberately no runnable current-base training command yet. Reuse `wnn.training` model/forward/state/input/optimizer/checkpoint/provenance seams and current per-cell infrastructure. Port only reviewed architecture modules from the frozen source, retaining current prediction safety and trainer changes. Bind Linux/CUDA environment and pinned Mamba build, data roots, output paths, actual device profile and per-cell owner before any fit. Do not execute the historical host runner as this CP30 design.

10. **Evidence to return.** Exact current source and inherited module pins; data/config/split/environment identities; architecture/parameter/FLOP counts; per-cell row/update/checkpoint identity, losses, LR, preclip norms, clipping/nonfinite counts, time and peak memory; complete predictions/official grades and paired uncertainty. Return weights separately from evidence with SHA256 manifests and approved storage locations. Profile/support work must be reported separately from scientific fits; failed cells never become zero scores or silent exclusions.

11. **Results and trace.** No model or performance result. The old source branches were successfully pushed and their remote tips verified; independent source review found the legacy integration and precision gaps described above. Tests, model imports, training, inference and profiles were not run locally. The published source map below also preserves complete causal-smoothing code on its own branch without force-updating PR #9. No CPU endpoint or competition upload is supplied.

title: [Experiment] Current-superbatch WP gradient replay
body:
# [Experiment] E-CURRENT-MOMENT-WP-20261018: current-superbatch weighted-Pearson replay

1. **Status, lineage and owner.** Proposal only: no implementation, adapter, clean registry binding, profile, fit, or grade. This is a narrow continuation of H-055; the experiment ID is `E-CURRENT-MOMENT-WP-20261018`. Pinned source: `1d57ed815c18eb278bcdd0207369b200970b28fb`. The receiving run owner is unassigned; the proposal branch is experiment/current-moment-wp-replay. Reuse the canonical GRU factory, but its exact model/input/LR registry entries remain unbound. `training_authorized=false`; `launch_ready=false`. The shared publication registers this continuation and experiment in the append-only ledgers.

2. **Why it should work.** Per-chunk Pearson can be degenerate when a chunk's target is constant; a decayed pooled-moment objective instead mixes statistics from earlier parameter states and does not give those earlier outputs the current objective's exact derivative. The candidate forms the official clipped weighted-Pearson objective over all eligible rows in one fixed 64-complete-sequence superbatch, at one frozen parameter state, then replays the same truncated chunks and applies cached output derivatives before one update. Unlike the separate H-RR17-19 adaptive-TBPTT continuation, this keeps K=500 and every detach boundary fixed; it changes only the objective-gradient estimator. Because the WMSE control shares the same 64-sequence macrostep, this comparison tests the objective conditional on that macrostep, not whether the larger macrostep beats the canonical training schedule. Predicted first evidence is agreement between the analytic output gradient, an autograd/finite-difference oracle, and deterministic replay on small synthetic cases; only then could a matched endpoint comparison test quality. Strong alternatives are that WMSE optimizes this recurrent model better, that macrobatch correlation is too noisy, or that clipped rows carry too little useful gradient. The discriminating control is the same macrostep and row population trained with canonical WMSE; no per-chunk-correlation or EMA arm is proposed.

3. **Compute advantage.** The candidate adds a graphless forward and a replay/backward forward, plus an ephemeral output-gradient buffer, relative to ordinary one-pass WMSE accumulation. Both arms use the same large macrostep and optimizer-update count, so the comparison does not silently change cadence. Cost and memory are unknown until an actual-device profile. A useful future result requires paired WP delta at least `+0.0005` and total candidate fit time no more than `2x` the matched control; these are proposed gates, not measurements or a scaling law. There is no teacher/cache generation or serving-time overhead.

4. **Frozen comparison.** Two arms: (A) label-only canonical WMSE control; (B) current-superbatch `clip2-WP` loss with two-pass output-gradient replay. Each paired fold/seed cell starts from the same cold initialization within the pair; different cells use their own seeds. No teacher, distillation target or warm parent is used; normal sequence-local GRU state is carried across chunks and reset only at sequence boundaries. No target/prediction cache persists across macrosteps. Only the candidate's temporary within-step output-gradient buffer is retained, then discarded.

   Both arms process identical sequence groups and row order: 64 complete 20,000-row sequences per superbatch, with the final partial superbatch included and scored on its actual eligible rows. Both perform one optimizer update per superbatch, for the same six epochs and update count; use the fixed epoch-5 endpoint. Within each sequence, carry recurrent state across K=500-row TBPTT chunks, detach at each chunk boundary, and reset at the sequence boundary. Replay records/restores the detached boundary states and RNG so its second pass matches the graphless pass before the single update. This is exact only for the fixed superbatch and its truncated graph, not for the full training fold or full BPTT, and not an average of per-chunk metrics.

   The candidate clips prediction and target to `[-2,2]`, weights each eligible row by the absolute clipped target, calculates separate weighted Pearson coefficients for the two targets over the current superbatch, then minimizes their negative mean.
